Bradford Alexander Halsey (February 14, 1981 – October 31, 2014) was am American Major League Baseball pitcher. He played for the New York Yankees, Arizona Diamondbacks and Oakland Athletics. Halsey died on October 31, 2014, near his home in New Braunfels, Texas, at the age of 33. According to the local judge who ordered the autopsy, Halsey's fatal injuries were caused by either a jump or a fall from a 100-foot cliff on private property. His body was discovered below, on a small road going up to the cliff.

Bradley Scott Fittler (born 5 February 1972), sometimes nicknamed "Freddy", is an Australian professional rugby league coach and former player. He is the current head coach of the New South Wales State of Origin team. He played mostly as a five-eighth. His career lasted from 1989 to 2004. He played for the Penrith Panthers until 1995 and later for the Sydney Roosters. He also coached the Roosters from 2007 to 2009. Fittler was born in Auburn, New South Wales. He is of German ancestry. He has three children; two of whom with his partner Marie Liarris.

Bradley David Ausmus (born April 14, 1969) is a former baseball catcher and manager. He played for the San Diego Padres, Detroit Tigers, Houston Astros, and Los Angeles Dodgers. He made his Major League Baseball debut in 1993 and retired from playing after the 2010 season. He was managed Detroit from 2014 to 2017.

Bradley James Haddin was born 23 October, 1977 in Cowra, New South Wales. He was an Australian cricketer who played 66 tests, 126 one-day internationals and 34 Twenty20 Internationals for Australia. He made his one-day international debut in January 2001 and became Australia's 400th test cricketer following the retirement of Adam Gilchrist in May 2008. He scored four test centuries (including three of them in The Ashes) and two one-day international centuries both against New Zealand. He also played for New South Wales in the Sheffield Shield. He retired from international cricket after the 2015 Ashes.

Bradley Scott Jones (born 19 March 1982) is an Australian former professional footballer who played as a goalkeeper. He played in England for Middlesbrough, Stockport County, Rotherham United, Blackpool, and Sheffield Wednesday.

Brad Robert Maxwell (born July 8, 1957 in Brandon, Manitoba) is a Canadian retired professional ice hockey defenceman. During his junior career he won the Memorial Cup in 1977 as a member of the New Westminster Bruins. Following that season Maxwell was selected seventh overall in the 1977 NHL Amateur Draft by the Minnesota North Stars. He spent time playing for Minnesota, the Quebec Nordiques, the Toronto Maple Leafs, the Vancouver Canucks and the New York Rangers before retiring in 1987.

Bradley Ralph (born October 17, 1980) is a Canadian retired professional ice hockey left winger and is the head coach of the Florida Everblades of the ECHL. He played in one National Hockey League game for the Phoenix Coyotes during the 2000–01 NHL season.

Brad Nessler (born June 3, 1956) is an American television sportscaster who currently calls college football and basketball games for CBS. He also called games for ABC, ESPN, and NFL Network calling Thursday Night Football games with Mike Mayock and Alex Flanagan. He started calling Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets basketball and Atlanta Falcons games. Nessler was also the voice of the Minnesota Vikings. Nessler also called college football, college basketball for Jefferson-Pilot and Miami Dolphins preseason. Nessler also called NFL, college football, men's and women's college basketball for CBS. During Nessler's time at ESPN, he also called NBA games for the ABC and NBA on ESPN before being removed from the broadcast team. He has been the #2 play-by-play announcer for ESPN Monday Night Football from 2006 and since 2010. He called Sebastian Janikowski's 63 yard field goal for the Oakland Raiders against the Denver Broncos at halftime in 2011.

Tyler Kluttz (born May 4, 1984 in Tega Cay, South Carolina) is an American professional wrestler and referee. He is best known for his time working for the WWE under the ring name Brad Maddox. He acted as the General Manager of Raw. On the August 20, 2012 episode of Raw, Kluttz debuted on the main roster and refereed a Divas battle royal. At Hell in a Cell, he refereed the main event between CM Punk and Ryback for the WWE Championship. Maddox turned heel for the first time when he gave Ryback a low blow and then fast-counted a pin for Punk which helped Punk retain his title. On the July 8 episode of Raw, Vickie Guerrero was fired when the fans voted that she had failed in her role of Raw Managing Supervisor. Maddox was then named as the new General Manager of Raw. FCW Florida Tag Team Championship (two times) (with Briley Pierce (one) and Rick Victor (one))

Bradley Glenn Richards (born May 2, 1980) is a Canadian former professional ice hockey centre. He played parts of sixteen seasons in the National Hockey League (NHL). He played for the Tampa Bay Lightning, Dallas Stars, New York Rangers, Chicago Blackhawks, and Detroit Red Wings. He also played for Ak Bars Kazan in the Russian Superleague (RSL). Richards would win the Stanley Cup with the Tampa Bay Lightning in 2004 and the Chicago Blackhawks in 2015. Before playing in the NHL, Richards played 1 season with the Notre Dame Hounds of the Saskatchewan Junior Hockey League (SJHL) and 3 seasons with the Rimouski Océanic of the Quebec Major Junior Hockey League (QMJHL). Over his QMJHL career, Richards was able to win the Jean Béliveau Trophy for being the league leader with 186 points, the Telus Cup for being the league's best offensive player, both the QMJHL and Canadian Hockey League Plus/Minus Awards, he was named as a First-Team All-Star in both the Quebec circuit, as well as the CHL and was also named the CHL Player of the Year and Leading Scorer. During the postseason, he was able to win the Guy Lafleur Trophy for being the MVP of the QMJHL playoffs and the Stafford Smythe Memorial Trophy for being the MVP of the 2000 Memorial Cup after the Océanic won both the QMJHL playoff title and the CHL national championship. Richards was drafted 64th overall by the Tampa Bay Lightning in the 1998 NHL Entry Draft. During the same draft, the Lightning also decided to draft Vincent Lecavalier who is Richard's best friend since the age of 14 and was his roommate at Athol Murray College of Notre Dame and his teammate with the Rimouski Océanic. In 2004, Richards won both the Conn Smythe and Lady Byng Memorial trophies and also won the Stanley Cup with the Lightning. During the 2004–05 NHL lockout, Richard decided to play for Ak Bars Kazan of the Russian Superleague (RSL). He also played for Team Canada during the 2006 Winter Olympics. When Canada was eliminated from the 2006 playoffs, the Lightning signed Richards to a five-year, $39 million contract. On February 26, 2008, the Lightning traded Richards and goaltender Johan Holmqvist to the Dallas Stars in exchange for Mike Smith, Jeff Halpern, Jussi Jokinen and a 4th round draft pick in the 2009 NHL Entry Draft. During the 2008 Playoffs, he was able to tie an NHL record after he scored four points in a single period in game 2 against the San Jose Sharks. He was able to record 16 goals and 48 points in 55 games in the 2008–09 NHL season before he broke his right wrist after being checked from Columbus Blue Jackets forward Jakub Voráček on February 16, 2009. On March 21, he returned to the lineup but he broke his other hand in the third period of a loss against San Jose. He did not return and the Stars missed the playoffs. On July 2, 2011, he signed a nine-year, $60 million contract with the New York Rangers after he became an unrestricted free agent. He scored his first NHL hat-trick against the Buffalo Sabres on April 19, 2013. On June 20, 2014, the Rangers bought out Richard's contract. On July 1, 2014, Richards signed a one-year, $2 million contract with the Chicago Blackhawks. He won the Stanley Cup with the Blackhawks after they defeated the Tampa Bay Lightning, in the 2015 Stanley Cup Finals. They won the Stanley Cup in six games. On July 1, 2015, Richards signed a one-year, $3 million contract with the Detroit Red Wings. On July 20, 2016, Richards announced that he was retiring from playing professional ice hockey.

Bradley Michael Hunt (born August 24, 1988) is a Canadian professional ice hockey defenceman. He currently plays for the Hershey Bears of the American Hockey League (AHL). He has also played for the Edmonton Oilers, St. Louis Blues, Nashville Predators, Vegas Golden Knights, Minnesota Wild, Vancouver Canucks, and Colorado Avalanche of the National Hockey League (NHL). Before playing in the NHL, Hunt played parts of 3 seasons with the Coquitlam Express of the British Columbia Hockey League (BCHL) and 4 years with the Bemidji State Beavers. With the Express, Hunt was named the team's Most Outstanding Defenceman twice and was named to the BCHL All-Star Game in 2007. Hunt was also successful in his time with the Beavers. He was named to CHA All-Tournament Team and helped them win the College Hockey America (CHA) tournament. By winning the tournament, the Beavers entered the 2009 NCAA Division I Men's Ice Hockey Tournament as the lowest seeded team. As the underdogs, the Beavers went on to defeat the Notre Dame Fighting Irish and Cornell Big Red to make it to the Frozen Four. The team eventually lost to the Miami RedHawks but Hunt was named to the NCAA Midwest Regional All-Tournament Team, All-CHA Rookie Team, All-CHA First Team, and was awarded the CHA Rookie of the Year. Hunt ended his time at Bemidji State as the team's all-time leader in defenceman scoring and defenceman power play goals. He was not drafted by an NHL team but signed a amateur tryout contract with the Chicago Wolves of the American Hockey League (AHL). Hunt was named to the 2013 AHL All-Star Game. On July 7, 2013, Hunt signed a two-year entry-level contract with the Edmonton Oilers. He was sent down and played most of his time with their AHL-affiliate Oklahoma City Barons. On January 3, 2014, Hunt made his NHL debut in a 5-2 loss against the Anaheim Ducks. On October 11, Hunt scored his first NHL goal in a 5-4 shootout loss against the Vancouver Canucks. On July 2, 2016, Hunt signed a one-year, two-way contract with the St. Louis Blues but only played 9 games with them. He was then placed on waivers and picked up by the Nashville Predators on January 16, 2017. On July 1, 2017, Hunt signed a two-year, one-way contract with the Vegas Golden Knights. He played 58 games with them. On January 21, 2019, the Golden Knights traded Hunt along with a sixth-round pick to the Minnesota Wild in exchange for a fifth-round pick in the 2019 NHL Entry Draft. On June 24, 2019, Hunt signed a two-year, $1.4 million extension to stay with the Wild. On July 28, 2021, Hunt signed a one-year, $800,000 contract with his home province Vancouver Canucks. He played 1 season with them. On July 15, 2022, Hunt signed a two-year, two-way contract with the Colorado Avalanche. He split time between the Avalanche and their AHL-affiliate Colorado Eagles. He was named to the AHL All-Star Classic but decided to instead play with the Avalanche. On August 2, 2024, Hunt signed a one-year contract with the Hershey Bears of the American Hockey League (AHL).

Brad Larsen (born June 28, 1977) is a Canadian professional head coach and former professional ice hockey left winger. He currently works as an assistant coach for the Calgary Flames of the National Hockey League (NHL). He also played parts of 8 seasons in the National Hockey League (NHL). He played for the Colorado Avalanche and Atlanta Thrashers. Before playing in the NHL, Larsen played four seasons with the Swift Current Broncos of the Western Hockey League (WHL). He had a successful career with the team. He was selected 53rd overall by the Ottawa Senators in the 1995 NHL entry draft. He did not play a game with them and was traded to the Colorado Avalanche. After not signing with them, he re-entered the 1997 NHL entry draft and was drafted 87th overall by the Avalanche. On March 21, 1998, Larsen made his NHL debut in a 2–0 win against the San Jose Sharks. On October 23, 2001, Larsen recorded his first point in the NHL, assisting on a Brian Willsie goal in a 5–1 win against the Carolina Hurricanes. On March 28, 2002, Larsen scored his first NHL goal against Evgeni Nabokov in a 3–2 win against the San Jose Sharks. He was waived by the Avalanche after the 2003–04 NHL season. On February 25, 2004, Larsen was claimed off waivers by the Atlanta Thrashers. He sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Chicago Wolves. He set a career high in games played with 75. He was later called up to the Thrashers and stayed there. On June 22, 2007, Larsen signed a two-year contract to stay with the Thrashers. On September 26, 2008, the Thrashers traded Larsen along with Ken Klee and Chad Painchaud to the Anaheim Ducks in exchange for Mathieu Schneider. He never played for the team because he dealt with too many injuries. On August 20, 2010, Larsen decided to retire from playing professional ice hockey. The same day, he signed a contract to become an assistant coach with the Springfield Falcons of the American Hockey League (AHL). He was later promoted to become the head coach of the Falcons. On June 10, 2021, Larsen was named head coach of the Columbus Blue Jackets. He served as the coach until he was fired on April 15, 2023. On June 11, 2024, Larsen was named as an assistant coach for the Calgary Flames.

Braden Holtby (born September 16, 1989) is a Canadian former professional ice hockey goaltender. He played a parts of 12 seasons in the National Hockey League (NHL). He played for the Washington Capitals, Vancouver Canucks, and Dallas Stars. Holtby won the Stanley Cup with the Capitals in 2018. He also won the Vezina Trophy as the league's best goaltender in 2016 and the William M. Jennings Trophy in 2017 for allowing the fewest goals in the league that year. Before playing in the NHL, Holtby played three seasons with the Saskatoon Blades of the Western Hockey League (WHL). He was selected 93rd overall by the Washington Capitals in the 2008 NHL entry draft. On October 20, 2008, he signed a three-year; entry-level contract with the Capitals. He played for both their AHL-affiliate Hershey Bears and the South Carolina Stingrays of the ECHL. On November 5, 2010, the Capitals called Holtby up and he made his NHL debut in a 5-3 win against the Boston Bruins. On March 9, 2011, he recorded his first NHL shutout in a 5-0 win against the Edmonton Oilers. Holtby helped the Capitals during the 2012 Stanley Cup playoffs, helping them reach the Eastern Conference semifinals before losing to the New York Rangers four games to three. On February 25, 2013, Holtby signed a two-year, $3.7 million contract extension to remain with the Capitals. He helped the team reach the playoffs again, making it to the Eastern Conference semifinals before they lost to the New York Rangers in a game 7 for a second time. On July 24, 2015, Holtby signed a 5-year, $30.5 million contract to remain with the Capitals. Holtby tied Martin Brodeur for the record of most wins in a single season record with 48. This came after a 5–1 win against the St. Louis Blues on April 9, 2016. He was named that year's Vezina Trophy winner for being the best goaltender in the NHL. Holtby backed up Philipp Grubauer and helped the Capitals make it to the Stanley Cup Final, where they defeated the Vegas Golden Knights four games to one to win their first Stanley Cup. Holtby, along with teammates Brett Connolly and Devante Smith-Pelly, refused to visit the White House in protest against the Trump administration. On October 9, 2020, Holtby signed a two-year, $8.6 million contract to join the Vancouver Canucks. He went on to play 21 games with the team. On July 27, 2021, the Canucks waived Holtby and bought out his contract. On July 28, 2021, Holtby signed a one-year, $2 million contract to join the Dallas Stars. On March 21, the Stars placed Holtby on long-term injured reserve list.

Charles Bradley Marsh (born March 31, 1958) is a Canadian former professional ice hockey defenceman. He played parts of 15 seasons in the National Hockey League (NHL). He played for the Atlanta Flames, Calgary Flames, Philadelphia Flyers, Toronto Maple Leafs, Detroit Red Wings, and Ottawa Senators. Marsh is a one-time All-Star, being named in 1993. Before playing in the NHL, Marsh played four seasons with the London Knights of the Ontario Major Junior Hockey League (OMJHL). During the 1976–77 season, he helped the Knights reach the finals for the J. Ross Robertson Cup but they lost to the Ottawa 67's four games to two. He was both drafted 11th overall by the Atlanta Flames in the 1978 NHL amateur draft. On October 11, 1978, Marsh made his NHL debut in a 4–4 tie with the Chicago Black Hawks. On October 13, he recorded his first NHL point, assisting on a Ken Houston goal in a 3–3 tie with the Washington Capitals. On October 13, 1979, Marsh scored his first NHL goal against Phil Myre in a 9–2 win against the Philadelphia Flyers. Marsh remained with the team when they moved from Atlanta to Calgary, Alberta. The now-Calgary Flames named Marsh as their first captain in franchise history. On November 11, 1981, the Flames traded Marsh to the Philadelphia Flyers in exchange for Mel Bridgman. In 1985, the Flyers named Marsh as an alternate captain of the team. He helped the team during the playoffs the next season. They defeated the New York Rangers, New York Islanders, and Montreal Canadiens. In the Finals, they ended up being defeated by the Edmonton Oilers four games to three. On October 3, 1988, Marsh was claimed off of waivers by the Toronto Maple Leafs. He played parts of three seasons with the Maple Leafs. On February 4, 1991, the Maple Leafs traded Marsh to the Detroit Red Wings in exchange for a 1991 eighth-round draft pick. He played parts of two seasons in Detroit, scoring 4 goals and recording 7 assists. On June 10, 1992, the Red Wings traded Marsh back to the Toronto Maple Leafs in exchange for cash considerations but he never played a game for them after the trade. The next month on July 20, the Maple Leafs traded Marsh to the Ottawa Senators for future considerations. During their first season in the league, the Senators named Marsh an alternate captain. In 1903, Marsh decided to retire from playing professional ice hockey.

Bradley Stuart (born November 6, 1979) is a Canadian former professional ice hockey defenceman. He played parts of 15 seasons in the National Hockey League (NHL). He played for the San Jose Sharks, Boston Bruins, Calgary Flames, Los Angeles Kings, Detroit Red Wings, and Colorado Avalanche. Stuart won the Stanley Cup with the Red Wings in 2008 Before playing in the NHL, Stuart played parts of four seasons with the Regina Pats and part of one season with the Calgary Hitmen of Western Hockey League (WHL). He was selected 3rd overall by the San Jose Sharks in the 1998 NHL entry draft. On October 2, 1999, Stuart made his NHL debut in a 5–3 win against the Calgary Flames. During the game, Stuart scored is first NHL goal against Grant Fuhr. On November 13, 2002, Stuart, as a restricted free agent, signed a three-year, $5 million contract to stay with the Sharks. On November 30, 2005, the Sharks traded Stuart along with Marco Sturm and Wayne Primeau to the Boston Bruins in exchange for Joe Thornton. He played parts of two seasons with the Bruins, scoring 17 goals and recording 31 assists. On February 10, 2007, the Bruins traded Stuart along with Wayne Primeau and a 2008 conditional fourth-round pick to the Calgary Flames in exchange for Andrew Ference and Chuck Kobasew. He only played 27 games with the Flames and recorded 5 assists. On July 3, 2003, Stuart decided to sign a one-year, $3.5-million contract to join the Los Angeles Kings. He played 63 games with the Kings, scoring 5 goals and recording 16 assists. On February 26, 2008, the Kings traded Stuart to the Detroit Red Wings in exchange for a 2008 second-round pick and a 2009 fourth-round pick. He helped the Red Wings during the playoffs where they defeated the Nashville Predators, Colorado Avalanche, and Dallas Stars. In the Finals, the Red Wings defeated the Pittsburgh Penguins four games to two to win the Stanley Cup. On July 1, 2008, Stuart signed a four-year, $15 million contract to remain with the Red Wings. He once again helped the Red Wings during the playoffs where they defeated the Columbus Blue Jackets, Anaheim Ducks, and Chicago Blackhawks. In the Finals, the Red Wings were defeated by the Pittsburgh Penguins four games to two. On June 10, 2012, the Red Wings traded Stuart to the San Jose Sharks in exchange for Andrew Murray and a 2014 conditional draft pick. On June 18, Stuart signed a three-year, $10.8 million contract to remain with the Sharks. Stuart was suspended by the league for three games after his elbow hit New York Rangers player Rick Nash on October 8, 2013. On July 1, 2014, the Sharks traded Stuart to the Colorado Avalanche in exchange for a 2016 second-round pick and a 2017 sixth-round pick. On September 29, 2014, Stuart signed a two-year contract to remain with the Avalanche. On December 18, 2014, Stuart played in his 1,000 career NHL game in a 1–0 loss against the Pittsburgh Penguins. On June 27, 2016, the Avalanche bought out he rest of Stuart's contract. In 2016, Stuart decided to retire from playing professional ice hockey.

Brad Lambert (born 19 December 2003) is a Finnish-Canadian professional ice hockey forward. He currently plays for the Manitoba Moose of the American Hockey League (AHL). Outside of the NHL, Lambert has also played for HIFK, JYP, and the Lahti Pelicans of the Liiga. Before playing in the NHL, Lambert played four regular season games with HIFK, parts of two season with JYP, and 25 regular season games with the Lahti Pelicans of the Liiga. He also played one season with the Seattle Thunderbirds of the Western Hockey League (WHL). He was drafted 30th overall by the Winnipeg Jets in the 2022 NHL entry draft. On 12 October 2022, Lambert signed a three-year entry-level contract to join the Jets. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Manitoba Moose. On 18 April 2024, the Jets called him up and Lambert made his NHL debut in a 4–2 win against the Vancouver Canucks. During the game, he recorded his first NHL point, assisting on a Gabriel Vilardi goal. On 1 November 2025, Lambert scored his first NHL goal against Artūrs Šilovs in a 5–2 win against the Pittsburgh Penguins. Lambert holds both Canadian and Finnish citizenship. His uncle Lane Lambert was also a professional hockey player, playing 283 games in the NHL and is the current coach of the Seattle Kraken.

Brad Marchand (born May 11, 1988) is a Canadian professional ice hockey left winger. He currently plays for the Florida Panthers of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the Boston Bruins. Marchand is a two-time Stanley Cup champion, winning with the Bruins in 2011 and with the Panthers in 2024. He is also a two-time All-Star, being named one in 2017 and 2018. Internationally, Marchand plays for Canada and he won a silver medal in 2026. Before playing in the NHL, Marchand played two seasons with the Moncton Wildcats, two seasons with the Val-d'Or Foreurs, and one season with the Halifax Mooseheads of the Quebec Major Junior Hockey League (QMJHL). He helped the Wildcats during the playoffs. They defeated the Victoriaville Tigres, Halifax Mooseheads, and Gatineau Olympiques before defeating the Quebec Remparts four games to two to win the President's Cup. This earned them a spot in the Memorial Cup tournament which Moncton also hosted. The Wildcats were eventually defeated by the Quebec Remparts 6–2 in the final game. He was drafted 71st overall by the Boston Bruins of the 2006 NHL entry draft. On March 2, 2025, Marchand signed a three-year entry-level contract to join the Vegas Golden Knights of the National Hockey League (NHL). He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Providence Bruins. On October 21, 2009, Boston called him up and Marchand made his NHL debut in a 3–2 win against the Nashville Predators. During the second period, he recorded his first NHL point after assisting on a Michael Ryder goal. On November 3, 2010, Marchand scored his first NHL goal short-handed against Jhonas Enroth in a 5–2 win against the Buffalo Sabres. He helped the Bruins during the playoffs. They defeated the Montreal Canadiens, Philadelphia Flyers, and Tampa Bay Lightning. They went on to defeat the Vancouver Canucks four games to three in the Final to win the Stanley Cup. On September 14, 2011, Marchand signed a two-year, $5 million contact to stay with the Bruins. On December 23, he recorded his first NHL hat-trick in a 8–0 win against the Florida Panthers. On January 16, 2015, the league suspended Marchand for two regular games and fined him $48,387 for slew-footing New York Rangers player Derick Brassard during a game. On November 2, 2015, he was named the NHL First Star of the Week. On November 13, he was fined $5,000 for roughing Colorado Avalanche player Gabriel Landeskog. On December 30, the league suspended him for three games and fined him $164,634 for clipping Ottawa Senators player Mark Borowiecki. On February 15, 2016, he was named the NHL Third Star of the Week. On September 26, 2016, Marchand signed a eight-year, $49 million contact to stay with the Bruins. On March 7, 2025, the Bruins traded Marchand to the Florida Panthers in exchange for 2027 conditional second-round draft pick. He helped the Panthers during the playoffs. They defeated the Tampa Bay Lightning, Toronto Maple Leafs, and Carolina Hurricanes. They went on to defeat the Edmonton Oilers four games to three in the Final to win the Stanley Cup.

Braden Schneider (born September 20, 2001) is a Canadian professional ice hockey defenceman. He currently plays for the New York Rangers of the National Hockey League (NHL). Before playing in the NHL, Schneider played parts of five seasons with the Brandon Wheat Kings of the Western Hockey League (WHL). He was drafted 19th overall by the New York Rangers of the 2020 NHL entry draft. On March 4, 2021, Schneider signed a three-year entry-level contract to join the Rangers. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Hartford Wolf Pack. On January 13, 2022, the Rangers called him up and Schneider made his NHL debut in a 3–0 win against the San Jose Sharks. During the third period, he scored his first NHL goal against Adin Hill. On July 13, 2024, Schneider signed a two-year, $4.4 million contract to stay with the Rangers. On July 13, 2026, Schneider signed a one-year, $5.5 million contract to stay with the Rangers.
Bradley Edward Wright-Phillips (born 12 March 1985) is an English former professional footballer who played as a striker. He is currently a host of MLS 360 on the MLS Season Pass.

Sir Bradley Marc Wiggins, CBE (born 28 April 1980) is a British cyclist. He was born in Ghent, Belgium. He grew up in Kilburn and Maida Vale, London. His mother Linda is English; his father was Australian cyclist Gary Wiggins (1952-2008). Wiggins won a bronze medal at the 2000 Summer Olympics, a gold medal, silver medal and bronze medal at the 2004 Summer Olympics, two gold medals at the 2008 Summer Olympics and a gold medal at the 2012 Summer Olympics. He won the 2012 Tour de France.

Brady Ellison (born October 27, 1988) is an American athlete. He is an archer who competed in the Summer Olympic Games. At the 2012 Summer Olympics, he was part of the men's archery team that won a silver medal.

Bradley Chase Walsh (born 4 June 1960) is an English actor, comedian, singer, and television presenter. People know him for his roles as Danny Baldwin in Coronation Street, DS Ronnie Brooks in Law & Order: UK, and Graham O'Brien in Doctor Who. Walsh also hosts the ITV game shows The Chase and Cash Trapped. Walsh is a former professional footballer for Brentford.

Brad Jones (racing driver) (born 1960), Australian racing driver Brad Jones (ice hockey) (born 1965), American former professional ice hockey left winger Brad Jones (soccer) (born 1982), Australian footballer Brad Jones (American football) (born 1986), American football linebacker Brad Jones (bassist) (born 1963), American jazz bassist Bradley Jones Jr. (born 1965), minority leader of the Massachusetts House of Representatives Bradley Jones (snooker player) (born 1974), English former snooker player The Cinema Snob, alter ego of internet humorist and film critic Brad Jones (born 1981)

Braeden Cootes (born February 9, 2007) is a Canadian professional ice hockey centre. He currently plays for the Prince Albert Raiders of the Western Hockey League (WHL). Before playing in the NHL, Cootes played four seasons with the Seattle Thunderbirds and one season with the Prince Albert Raiders of the Western Hockey League (WHL). On January 6, 2026, the Thunderbirds traded Cootes along with a 2026 fourth-round draft pick, a 2026 sixth-round draft pick, and a 2028 conditional second-round draft pick to the Prince Alberta Raiders in exchange for Ethan Bibeau, Knox Burton, Diego Gutierrez, Tripp Fischer, a 2026 first-round draft pick, a 2026 second-round draft pick, a 2027 third-round draft pick, and a 2028 first-round draft pick. He was drafted 15th overall by the Vancouver Canucks in the 2025 NHL entry draft. On July 9, 2025, Cootes signed a three-year entry-level contract to join the Canucks. On October 9, 2025, Cootes made his NHL debut in a 5–1 win against the Calgary Flames.

Brady Martin (born March 16, 2007) is a Canadian professional ice hockey centre. He currently plays for the Sault Ste. Marie Greyhounds of the Ontario Hockey League (OHL) and is a prospect of the Nashville Predators of the National Hockey League (NHL). Before playing in the NHL, Martin played parts of two seasons with the Sault Ste. Marie Greyhounds of the Ontario Hockey League (OHL). He was drafted 5th overall by the Nashville Predators in the 2025 NHL entry draft. On August 20, 2025, Martin signed a three-year entry-level contract to join the Predators. On January 3, 2025, the Predators called him up and Martin made his NHL debut in a 2–1 win against the Columbus Blue Jackets. Two days later on October 26, he recorded his first NHL point after assisting on a Filip Forsberg goal in a 3–2 overtime loss against the Utah Mammoth. After another game, the Predators sent Martin back down to play for the Greyhounds.

Brady Michael Skjei (born March 26, 1994) is an American professional ice hockey defenseman. He currently plays for the Nashville Predators of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the New York Rangers and Carolina Hurricanes. Before playing in the NHL, Skjei played two seasons with the U.S. National Team Development Program of the United States Hockey League (USHL) and three years with the Minnesota Golden Gophers of the Big Ten Conference (B1G). He was drafted 28th overall by the New York Rangers in the 2012 NHL entry draft. On April 1, 2015, Skjei signed a three-year entry-level contract to join the Rangers. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Hartford Wolf Pack. On December 15, 2015, Skjei made his NHL debut in a 4–2 win against the Edmonton Oilers. On April 16, 2016 during Game 2 Eastern Conference first round, he recorded his first NHL point when he assisted on a Derick Brassard goal in a 4–2 win against the Pittsburgh Penguins. On December 11, Skjei scored his first NHL goal against Cory Schneider in a 5–0 win against the New Jersey Devils. On July 28, 2018, Skjei signed a six-year, $31.5 million contract to stay with the Rangers. On February 24, 2020, the Rangers traded Skjei to the Carolina Hurricanes in exchange for a 2020 conditional first-round draft pick. He played parts of five seasons with the Hurricanes. On July 1, 2024, Skjei signed a seven-year, $49 million contract to join the Nashville Predators.

Braeden Tkachuk (born September 16, 1999) is an American professional ice hockey left winger. He currently plays for the Florida Panthers of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the Ottawa Senators. Tkachuk is a four-time All-Star, being named one in 2020, 2022, 2023, and 2024. Internationally, Tkachuk plays for the United States and won a gold medal in 2026. Before playing in the NHL, Tkachuk played two seasons with the U.S. National Development Team of the United States Hockey League (USHL) and one year with the Boston University Terriers of Hockey East. He had a successful time with his teams. With the Terriers, he was named to the All-Hockey East Rookie Team. He was drafted 4th overall by the Ottawa Senators of the 2018 NHL entry draft. On August 13, 2018, Tkachuk signed a three-year entry-level contract to join the Senators. On October 8, 2018, Tkachuk made his NHL debut in a 6–3 loss against the Boston Bruins. On October 10, Tkachuk scored his first two NHL goals against Calvin Pickard in a 7–4 loss against the Philadelphia Flyers. He also assisted on a Maxime Lajoie goal for a three point game. On December 11, 2021, he recorded his first NHL hat-trick in a 4–0 win against the Tampa Bay Lightning. On October 14, 2021, Tkachuk signed a seven-year, $57.5 million contract to stay with the Senators. On November 5, the team announced Tkachuk as the 10th captain in Senators franchise history. On June 21, 2026, the Senators traded Tkachuk to the Florida Panthers in exchange for a Florida's 2026 first-, 2029 first-, and 2027 second-round draft picks, as well as, the Tampa Bay Lightning's 2026 first-round draft pick which was held by the Panthers. Many Senators fans were angry with Tkachuk's trade and either traded in or destroyed their jerseys after his departure, especially after Tkachuk announced in April 2026 that he was committed to playing in Ottawa. Tkachuk comes from a hockey family. His father Keith played 18 seasons in the NHL and his older brother Matthew is his teammate on the Panthers. Both Brady and Matthew were born in Scottsdale, Arizona when their father played for the Phoenix Coyotes.

Braeden Bowman (born June 26, 2003) is a Canadian professional ice hockey right winger. He currently plays for the Vegas Golden Knights of the National Hockey League (NHL). Before playing in the NHL, Bowman played parts of four seasons with the Guelph Storm of the Ontario Hockey League (OHL). He was not drafted by an NHL team. On March 2, 2025, Bowman signed a three-year entry-level contract to join the Vegas Golden Knights of the National Hockey League (NHL). He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Henderson Silver Knights. On November 13, 2025, the Golden Knights called him up and Bowman made his NHL debut in a 4–3 overtime loss against the New York Islanders. Two days later on November 15, Bowman scored his first NHL goal on the powerplay against Joel Hofer in a 4–1 win against the St. Louis Blues. On September 10, 2026, Bowman signed a eight-year, $58.8 million contract to stay with the Knights.
Cláudio Ibrahim Vaz Leal (born 4 April 1964 in Bagé, Brazil), better known as Branco, is a former Brazilian football player. He has played for Brazil national team.

Wesley Branch Rickey (December 20, 1881 – December 9, 1965) was an American Major League Baseball (MLB) executive. He was elected to the Baseball Hall of Fame in 1967. He was best known for breaking Major League Baseball's color barrier by signing African American player Jackie Robinson, for drafting the first Afro-Hispanic superstar, Roberto Clemente, for creating the framework for the modern minor league farm system, for encouraging the Major Leagues to add new teams through his involvement in the proposed Continental League, and for introducing the batting helmet.

Brandon Louis Bochenski (born April 4, 1982) is a Kazakhstani-American former professional ice hockey player. He was picked by the Ottawa Senators with the 223rd overall pick in the 2001 NHL Entry Draft. He played in the NHL for many teams including the Ottawa Senators from 2004-2006, Chicago Blackhawks from 2005-2007, Boston Bruins from 2006-2008, Anaheim Ducks in 2007, Nashville Predators in 2007 and the Tampa Bay Lightning from 2008-2010 before leaving North America to sign a one-year contract with the Kontinental Hockey League's, Barys Astana.

Brandon Bass (born April 30, 1985) is an American basketball player of the National Basketball Association (NBA). He is with the Boston Celtics. He played for LSU in college. He is a 6'8", 250 lb power forward. On July 26, 2007, Bass agreed to play for the Dallas Mavericks. He signed through the 2008-09 season with a $1.59 million contract. On July 10, 2009, Bass signed a contract with the Orlando Magic. He was traded to the Boston Celtics in December 2011 for Glen Davis and Von Wafer. In July 2016, Brandon Bass agreed one-year deal with the Los Angeles Clippers. In August 2017, signed a one-year, $2 million deal with the Liaoning Leopards.

Brandon Bollig (born January 31, 1987, in Saint Charles, Missouri) is an American retired professional ice hockey center. He currently plays for the Calgary Flames of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the Chicago Blackhawks. He was not drafted by a team but the Blackhawks signed Bollig to a two-year entry-level contract and put him on their AHL farm team, the Rockford IceHogs. He played 2 seasons with the IceHogs and was called up to the Blackhawks on February 28, 2012. He scored his first NHL goal on April 14, 2012, against Mike Smith of the Phoenix Coyotes in a playoff game. Bollig also portrayed Will Cross, age 12 in the 2002 film Defiance. On June 24, 2013, He won the Stanley Cup with the Blackhawks after they defeated the Boston Bruins 4 games to 2 in the 2013 Stanley Cup Finals. On June 28, 2014 at the 2014 NHL Entry Draft, the Blackhawks traded Bollig to the Calgary Flames in exchange for the 83rd overall pick in the draft.

Brandon Joel Gaetano Borello (born 25 July 1995) is an Australian soccer player. He plays for the Western Sydney Wanderers in the A-League Men and for the Australia men's national soccer team (nicknamed the "Socceroos"). Y-League BRFC Player of the Year: 2013–14

Brandon Roy (born July 23, 1984 in Seattle, Washington) is a retired professional basketball player. He played for the Portland Trail Blazers of the National Basketball Association (NBA) from 2006 to 2011. He won the NBA Rookie of the Year Award in 2007, and was chosen as an All Star in 2008, 2009, and 2010. Roy played college basketball for four years at the University of Washington. The Minnesota Timberwolves chose him with the sixth pick in the 2006 NBA Draft, but traded him to the Trail Blazers later that night. On December 9, 2011, Roy said that he would retire from basketball because of knee problems.

Brandon Jennings (born September 23, 1989 in Compton, California) is an American former professional basketball player. He played parts of eleven seasons in the National Basketball Association (NBA). He played for the Milwaukee Bucks, Detroit Pistons, Orlando Magic, New York Knicks, and Washington Wizards. He played as a point guard. for the Milwaukee Bucks of the National Basketball Association (NBA). He also played basketball in Italy for Lottomatica Roma of the Italian Lega A. He last played for Zenit Saint Petersburg of the VTB United League. He was released after only 10 games because he criticized the team's management in an Instagram post. Jennings retired from playing professional basketball in 2018.

Brandon Saad (born October 27, 1992, in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania) is an American professional ice hockey left winger. He currently plays for the Columbus Blue Jackets of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the Chicago Blackhawks. He was drafted by the Blackhawks with the 43rd overall pick in the 2011 NHL Entry Draft. Saad scored his first career NHL goal on February 5, 2013, against Antti Niemi of the San Jose Sharks. Before going to the NHL, he played 2 seasons with the Saginaw Spirit of the Ontario Hockey League. He won the gold medal with the United States at the 2010 IIHF World U18 Championships. On June 24, 2013, He won the Stanley Cup with the Blackhawks after they defeated the Boston Bruins 4 games to 2 in the 2013 Stanley Cup Finals. On June 30, 2015, the Blackhawks traded Saad along with Alex Broadhurst and Michael Paliotta, to the Columbus Blue Jackets in exchange for Jeremy Morin, Marko Daňo, Artem Anisimov, Corey Tropp and a fourth-round draft pick in 2016.

Brandon Pirri (born April 10, 1991, in Toronto, Ontario) is a Canadian professional ice hockey centre. He currently plays the Vegas Golden Knights of the National Hockey League (NHL). Before he played in the NHL, Pirri played in the Ontario Junior Hockey League for the Streetsville Derbys and the Georgetown Raiders. He also played at the Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute in the ECAC Hockey conference. He was drafted by the Blackhawks with the 59th overall pick in the 2009 NHL Entry Draft. He spends most of his time with the Blackhawks AHL farm team, the Rockford IceHogs. On March 2, 2014, the Blackhawks traded Pirri to the Florida Panthers for a 2014 3rd round pick and a 2016 5th round pick.

Brandon Douglas Moss (born September 16, 1983) is an American Professional baseball player. He is currently a free agent. Moss has played for the Boston Red Sox, Pittsburgh Pirates, Oakland Athletics, and the Philadelphia Phillies. He was born 16 September 1983 in Monroe, Georgia. He graduated from Loganville High School in Loganville, Georgia. Moss was drafted in the 8th round of the 2002 Major League Baseball Draft by the Boston Red Sox. Moss began playing minor league ball, starting with the Gulf Coast Red Sox. He then played for the Lowell Spinners, Augusta GreenJackets, and Sarasota Red Sox. He spent two years with the Double-A Portland Sea Dogs in 2005 and 2006. He then played for the Triple-A Pawtucket Red Sox.

Brandon Michael Harry Yip (; born April 25, 1985) is a Canadian-Chinese professional ice hockey right winger. He currently plays for the Kunlun Red Star of the Kontinental Hockey League (KHL). He also played parts of six years in the National Hockey League (NHL) for the Colorado Avalanche, Nashville Predators, and Phoenix Coyotes. Before playing in the NHL, Yip played parts of 2 seasons with the Coquitlam Express of the British Columbia Hockey League (BCHL) and four years at Boston University with the Terriers. While playing with the Terriers, Yip would be named the Hockey East Rookie of the Year and would win the NCAA Men's Ice Hockey Championship. He was drafted 239th overall by the Colorado Avalanche in the 2004 NHL Entry Draft. On July 22, 2009, Yip signed a one-year; entry level contract with the Colorado Avalanche. On December 19, Yip made his NHL debut in a 5-2 win against the Columbus Blue Jackets. On December 22, he would score his first NHL goal on Jonas Hiller in a 4-2 loss against the Anaheim Ducks. On July 7, 2010, he would sign a two-year; $1.5 million contract extension with the Avalanche. On January 19, 2012, Yip would be claimed off waivers by the Nashville Predators. He would sign with the Predators on June 21, 2012. On July 19, 2013, Yip decided to sign a one-year; two way contract with the Phoenix Coyotes. He would spend time between the Coyotes and their AHL-affiliate team, the Portland Pirates. In 2015 and 2016, Yip move to Germany and would play for Adler Mannheim and Düsseldorfer EG of the Deutsche Eishockey Liga (DEL). On July 26, 2021, Yip signed with Kunlun Red Star of the Kontinental Hockey League (KHL). He made the move because he wanted to reconnect with his Chinese heritage and wanted to play for the China men's national ice hockey team at the 2022 Winter Olympics.

Brandon Jenner (born June 4, 1981) is an American singer-songwriter and television personality. He is known for his appearances in Keeping Up with the Kardashians, The Princes of Malibu, and The Hills: New Beginnings. Jenner was born in June 4, 1981 in Los Angeles, California to television personality and Olympic gold medalist Caitlyn Jenner, and actress and songwriter Linda Thompson. In 2005, he formed a band with his then girlfriend Leah Felder called Big Dume. In 2012, Jenner and Felder formed indie pop group Brandon & Leah. They released two albums, Cronies (2013) and Together (2014). The group broke-up after their divorce.

Brandon Clarke (September 19, 1996 – May 11, 2026) was a Canadian-American professional basketball player. He played in the National Basketball Association (NBA) for the Memphis Grizzlies from 2019 until 2025. He played college basketball for the San Jose State Spartans and Gonzaga Bulldogs. He was named to the NBA All-Rookie First Team in 2020. On April 1, 2026, Clarke was arrested in Cross County, Arkansas for having over 200 grams of kratom and drug trafficking. He was chased by police officers and drove over 100mph before being arrested. Clarke died on May 11, 2026, in Los Angeles, California, at the age of 29. His cause of death was confirmed to be an accidental overdose of cocaine, heroin, and other prescription drugs.

Brandon Montour (born April 11, 1994) is a Canadian professional ice hockey defenceman. He currently plays for the Seattle Kraken of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the Anaheim Ducks, Buffalo Sabres, and Florida Panthers. Montour is a one-time Stanley Cup champion, winning with Panthers in 2024. Before playing in the NHL, Montour played parts of two seasons with the Waterloo Black Hawks of the United States Hockey League (USHL) and one year with the UMass Minutemen of Hockey East. He had a successful time with his teams. With the Black Hawks, he finished the 2013–14 season scoring 14 goals and recording 48 assists for 62 points. He was named both the Player of the Year and Defenceman of the Year for his efforts and was also named to the All-Star Game and First All-Star Team. With the Minutemen, he was named to the Hockey East All-Rookie Team in 2015. He was drafted 55th overall by the Anaheim Ducks in the 2014 NHL entry draft. On March 16, 2015, Montour signed a three-year entry-level contract to join the Ducks. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliates Norfolk Admirals and San Diego Gulls. On December 29, 2016, the Ducks called him up and Montour made his NHL debut in a 3–1 win against the Calgary Flames. On February 4, 2017, Montour scored his first NHL goal against Ben Bishop in a 3–2 shootout loss to the Tampa Bay Lightning. On July 24, 2018, Montour signed a two-year, $6.775 million contract to stay with the Ducks. On February 24, 2019, the Ducks traded Montour to the Buffalo Sabres in exchange for Brendan Guhle and a 2019 conditional first-round draft pick. He played parts of three seasons with the Sabres. On April 10, 2021, the Sabres traded Montour to the Florida Panthers in exchange for a 2021 third-round draft pick. He helped the Panthers when they went on a run in the playoffs. They defeated the Tampa Bay Lightning, Boston Bruins, and New York Rangers. They went on to defeat the Edmonton Oilers four games to three in the Final to win the first Stanley Cup in Panthers franchise history. He played parts of four seasons with the Panthers. On July 1, 2024, Montour signed a seven-year, $49.98 million contract to join the Seattle Kraken. Montour is of Mohawk descent. He grew up in Ohsweken, Ontario, within the Six Nations of the Grand River reserve.

Brandt Clarke (born February 9, 2003) is a Canadian professional ice hockey defenceman. He currently plays for the Los Angeles Kings of the National Hockey League (NHL). Outside of the NHL, Clarke has played for HC Nové Zámky of the Slovak Extraliga. Before playing in the NHL, Clarke played three seasons with the Barrie Colts and one season with HC Nové Zámky of the Slovak Extraliga. He had a successful time with his teams. He was named to the CHL First All-Star Team, OHL First All-Rookie Team, OHL Second All-Star Team, and the OHL First All-Star Team. He was drafted 8th overall by the Los Angeles Kings in the 2021 NHL entry draft. On August 10, 2021, Clarke signed a three-year entry-level contract to join the Kings. On October 13, 2022, Clarke made his NHL debut in a 4–1 loss against the Seattle Kraken. On October 20, he recorded his first NHL point after assisting on a Carl Grundström goal in a 6–1 loss against the Pittsburgh Penguins. On February 17, 2024, Clarke scored his first NHL goal and the overtime winner against Linus Ullmark in a 5–4 overtime win against the Boston Bruins. Clarke's older brother Graeme Clarke is also a professional hockey player.

Brandon Tanev (born December 31, 1991) is a Canadian professional ice hockey left winger. He currently plays for the Utah Mammoth of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the Winnipeg Jets, Pittsburgh Penguins, and Seattle Kraken. Before playing in the NHL, Tanev played one season with the Surrey Eagles of the British Columbia Hockey League (BCHL) and four years with the Providence Friars of Hockey East. He was not drafted by an NHL team. On March 30, 2016, Tanev signed a one-year, $925,000 entry-level contract to join the Winnipeg Jets of the National Hockey League (NHL). On April 5, 2016, Tanev made his NHL debut in a 2–1 overtime win against the Anaheim Ducks. On July 21, Tanev signed a one-year, $874,125 contract to stay with the Jets. On November 3, he recorded his first NHL point after assisting on a Marko Daňo goal in a 4–3 overtime loss against the Washington Capitals. On November 4, Tanev scored his first two NHL goals against Petr Mrázek in a 5–3 win against the Detroit Red Wings. On July 10, 2017, Tanev signed a one-year, $874,125 contract to stay with the Jets. On March 27, 2018, Tanev recorded his first NHL hat-trick in a 5–4 shootout win against the Boston Bruins. On July 22, Tanev signed a one-year, $1.15 million contract to stay with the Jets. On July 1, 2019, Tanev signed a six-year, $21 million contract to join the Pittsburgh Penguins. He played parts of two seasons with the Penguins. On July 21, 2021, the Penguins left Tanev unprotected in the 2021 NHL expansion draft and he was selected by the Seattle Kraken. On December 18, it was announced by the Kraken that Tanev had torn his anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) and had to miss the rest of the season because he needed surgery to repair it. He played four seasons with the Kraken. On March 7, 2025, the Kraken traded Tanev back to the Winnipeg Jets in exchange for a 2027 second-round draft pick. Tanev scored 1 goal and recorded 4 assists in 19 regular season games during his return to the Jets. On July 1, 2025, Tanev signed a six-year, $21 million contract to join the Utah Mammoth. Tanev's older brother Christopher Tanev is also a professional hockey in the NHL. Tanev's wide-eyed expression in his player headshot became a viral meme with Tanev recreating the face for his time with the Kraken and Jets. It has also been recreated by other athletes like NFL running back DeeJay Dallas.

Brandon Mitchell Carlo (born November 26, 1996) is an American professional ice hockey defenseman. He currently plays for the St. Louis Blues of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the Boston Bruins and Toronto Maple Leafs. Before playing in the NHL, Carlo played four season with the Tri-City Americans of the Western Hockey League (WHL). He was drafted 37th overall by the Boston Bruins of the 2015 NHL entry draft. On September 25, 2015, Carlo signed a three-year entry-level contract to join the Bruins. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Providence Bruins. On October 13, 2016, Boston called him up and Carlo made his NHL debut in a 6–3 win against the Columbus Blue Jackets. During the third period, he recorded his first NHL point after assisting on a Brad Marchand goal. On October 17, Carlo scored his first NHL goal against Connor Hellebuyck in a 4–1 win against the Winnipeg Jets. On July 14, 2021, Carlo signed a six-year, $24.6 million contract to stay with the Bruins. On March 7, 2025, the Bruins traded Carlo to the Toronto Maple Leafs in exchange for Fraser Minten, a 2025 fourth-round draft pick, and a 2026 conditional first-round draft pick. He recorded ten assists in two seasons with the Leafs. On June 27, 2026, the Leafs traded Carlo to the St. Louis Blues in exchange for two 2026 third-round draft picks. Carlo is a non-denominational Christian and has 2 Corinthians 5:7, "Live by faith not by sight" tattooed on his arm.

Antenor Lucas, better known as Brandãozinho (born in Campinas, Brazil, June 9, 1925 – died in São Paulo, Brazil, April 4, 2000) was a former Brazilian football player. He has played for Brazil's national team. Brandaõzinho was widely regarded as one of the finest defenders and midfielders ever to play the game. He was renowned for his marking, tackling, dribbling, pressure, anticipation and his short and long passes. He also performs mainly covering and marking duties, positioning himself in front of the defensive line. Brandanzinho began his career at the Campinas club in 1940, then in 1943 he moved to another São Paulo club, Portuguesa Santista. In 1949, Brandanzinho moved to Portuguesa Desportos, where he made his debut on September 1, 1949 in a friendly game with the Palmeiras club, which ended in a 1-3 defeat for Portuguesa. In an official match for Portuguesa, Brandanzinho played for the first time 10 days later: on September 11, in the São Paulo championship, Portuguesa met Corinthians”, the game again ended with the defeat of the Brandanzinho club with a score of 1-3, but Portuguesa had an excuse, his player was injured and left the field, and substitutions were not yet practiced in those years. On September 26, the first victory of Portugues came, with a score of 4-1, Brandanzinho's former club Portuguesa Santista was beaten, one of the goals on Brandanzinho's account, which became the player's first goal in Desportos. Brandanzinho played for Portuguesa Desportos for 7 years, winning two Rio Sao Paulo tournaments with the club in 1952 and 1955. In 1952, he made his debut in official matches as part of the Brazilian national team at the Pan American Games tournament, where the Brazilian team won. The following year, he played as part of the national team at the South American Championship in Peru in 1953, where he won silver with the team. In 1954, as part of the national team, he participated in the world championship in Switzerland, where he played 3 games. His last game was in 1955 during the Copa Oswaldo Cruz against Chile. During his career in the national team, which lasted 3 years, he played 18 matches in its uniform. After finishing his performances on the football fields, Brandanzinho worked for some time in the police, and for 30 years he worked as a journalist for the newspaper "Detran de São Paulo". For a long time he worked as a mathematics teacher at school. Brandanzinho died on April 4, 2000 in the city of Sao Paulo.

Branko Elsner (23 November 1929 – 17 November 2012) was a Slovenian football manager and player. He is best known for being the manager of the Austria national team twice. As manager he had his first success with NK Olimpija Ljubljana. Then he went to Austria and became coach of Wacker Innsbruck. As manager he won the Austrian Bundesliga twice (1972, 1975) and the Austrian Cup (1970, 1975). In 1975, and from 1985 to 1988, he was manager of the Austria national football team. In 1982, he did a doctorate and during the 1990s, he was a teacher at the University of Ljubljana. His son Marko Elsner and grandsons Luka Elsner and Rok Elsner were professional footballers.

Branko Tesanić (10 February 1920 – 25 August 1984) was a Yugoslav football referee. He refereed at the 1962 FIFA World Cup. During the 1963–64 European Cup semi-finals between Inter Milan and Borussia Dortmund, he controversially didn't send off Luis Suárez after he violently kicked and injured a Borussia Dortmund player.
Bransby Beauchamp Cooper (15 March 1844 – 7 August 1914) was an Australian cricketer. He played in one Test match in 1877. He played 50 first-class matches in total.

Braulio Armando Lara (20 December 1988 – 20 April 2019) was a Dominican professional baseball player. He played as a pitcher. In the United States, he was signed to the Tampa Bay Rays, the Miami Marlins and the Washington Nationals. In 2016, he played with the SK Wyverns of the KBO League in South Korea. He later played for the Mexican teams Sultanes de Monterrey and Generales de Durango. He was born in Baní, Peravia Province. Lara died in a car accident on 20 April 2019 in Baní. He was 30.

Braulio Enrique Musso Reyes (8 March 1930 – 18 June 2025) was a Chilean footballer. He played as a left winger for Universidad de Chile between 1951 and 1968. He was also capped 14 times for Chile, and was part of their team at the 1962 FIFA World Cup. Musso died on 18 June 2025, at the age of 95. Chilean Primera División: 1959, 1962, 1964, 1965, 1967

Windham Lawrence Rotunda (May 23, 1987 – August 24, 2023), better known by his ring name Bray Wyatt was an American professional wrestler. He was known as the leader of a stable with Luke Harper and Erick Rowan called The Wyatt Family. Wyatt was a three-time world champion. He first wrestled in WWE from 2009 to 2011 where he competed under the name Husky Harris and was a part of the stable, The Nexus. He competed on the 2nd season of WWE NXT but was eliminated 5th. Rotunda stayed in WWE's developmental territory, Florida Championship Wrestling (FCW), and made his debut as Bray Wyatt in FCW in April 2012. He stayed in FCW through its name change to NXT Wrestling (now WWE NXT), and returned to the main WWE roster in July 2013. The Wyatt Family quickly became some of the company's biggest heels ("bad guys"). In 2019, Wyatt started wresting as The Fiend. On August 24, 2023, Rotunda died from a heart attack. He had been out with a private illness since February which was later said to be COVID-19. Brayden Luke McNabb (born January 28, 1991) is a Canadian ice hockey defenceman. He currently plays for the Vegas Golden Knights of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the Buffalo Sabres and Los Angeles Kings. Before playing in the NHL, McNabb played parts of 4 seasons with the Kootenay Ice of the Western Hockey League (WHL). McNabb played for Team Canada during the 2009 IIHF World U18 Championships and won a gold medal with Canada at the 2008 Ivan Hlinka Memorial Tournament. He was drafted 66th overall by the Buffalo Sabres in the 2009 NHL Entry Draft. He signed a three-year entry level contract with the Sabres on May 18, 2011. On November 26, 2011, McNabb made his NHL debut in a 5–1 win against the Washington Capitals. On December 26, 2011, he scored his first NHL goal against Tomáš Vokoun of the Washington Capitals in a 4-2 win. On March 5, 2014, the Sabres traded McNabb, along with Jonathan Parker and two draft picks, to the Los Angeles Kings in exchange for Hudson Fasching and Nicolas Deslauriers.

Braxton Berrios (born October 6, 1995) is an American football wide receiver for the Miami Dolphins of the National Football League (NFL). He played college football at Miami (FL). He was a star athlete at Leesville Road High School in Raleigh, North Carolina where he played quarterback. He was drafted by the New England Patriots in the sixth round of the 2018 NFL Draft.

Brayden Michael Schenn (born August 22, 1991) is a Canadian professional ice hockey centre. He currently plays for the St. Louis Blues of the National Hockey League (NHL) and serves as their captain. Schenn won the Stanley Cup with the Blues in 2019. Before playing in the NHL, Schenn played three seasons with the Brandon Wheat Kings of the Western Hockey League (WHL). He had a successful time with the Wheat Kings. In his first year with the team, Schenn won the Jim Piggott Memorial Trophy for WHL Rookie of the Year, and was also named to the Canadian Hockey League (CHL) All-Rookie Team. In his second season, he was named to the Eastern Conference Second All-Star Team and played in the CHL Top Prospects Game. He was selected 5th overall by the Los Angeles Kings in the 2009 NHL entry draft. On January 10, 2011, the Wheat Kings traded Schenn to the Saskatoon Blades in exchange for draft picks and prospects. On November 26, 2009, the Kings called Schenn up on emergency and he played in his first NHL game in a 4–1 loss to the Vancouver Canucks. On March 3, 2010, Schenn signed a three-year contract to stay with the Kings. On June 23, 2011, the Kings traded Schenn along with Wayne Simmonds and a 2012 second round pick to the Wayne Simmonds in exchange for Mike Richards and Rob Bordson. He was sent down to their AHL-affiliate Adirondack Phantoms after injuring his shoulder. On January 2, 2012, during the NHL Winter Classic, Schenn scored his first NHL goal against Henrik Lundqvist in a 3–2 loss to the New York Rangers. On February 29, 2016, Schenn scored his first NHL hat-trick in a 5–3 win against the Calgary Flames. On July 25, 2016, Schenn signed a four-year, $20.5 million contract to remain with the Flyers. On June 23, 2017, the Flyers traded Schenn to the St. Louis Blues in exchange for Jori Lehterä, a 2017 first-round pick and a conditional 2018 first-round pick. He had a very successful first year with the team, recording career highs in points, assists, and goals. He was also named to the 2018 National Hockey League All-Star Game. Schenn helped the team make it to the 2019 Stanley Cup Playoffs. They were able to make it all the way to the Finals where they defeated the Boston Bruins four games to three and win the first Stanley Cup in franchise history. On October 4, 2019, Schenn signed an eight-year, $52 million contract to remain with the Blues. On September 19, 2023, the Blues named Schenn as the 24th captain in their history. Schenn's older brother, Luke, also played in the NHL.

Brayden Trevor Yager (born January 3, 2005) is a Canadian professional ice hockey centre. He currently plays for the Manitoba Moose of the American Hockey League (AHL). Before playing in the NHL, Yager played parts of five seasons with the Moose Jaw Warriors and part of one season with the Lethbridge Hurricanes of the Western Hockey League (WHL). He had a successful time with his teams. He finished his rookie season scoring 34 goals and recording 25 assists for 59 points in 63 regular season games. He won the Jim Piggott Memorial Trophy for being the WHL's most proficient rookie and he was also named the CHL Rookie of the Year for his production. He helped the Warriors during the playoffs. They defeated the Brandon Wheat Kings, Swift Current Broncos and Saskatoon Blades before defeating and sweeping the Portland Winterhawks four games to zero to win the first Ed Chynoweth Cup in Warriors franchise history. This earned them a spot in the Memorial Cup tournament. The Warriors went on to be defeated in the semi-final game 7–1 by the eventual champions Saginaw Spirit. He was drafted 14th overall by the Pittsburgh Penguins in the 2023 NHL entry draft. On July 25, 2024, Yager signed a three-year entry-level contract to join the Penguins. He never played a game for the Penguins. On August 22, 2024, the Penguins traded Yager to the Winnipeg Jets in exchange for Rutger McGroarty. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Manitoba Moose. On April 13, 2026, the Jets called him up and Yager made his NHL debut in a 6–2 loss against the Vegas Golden Knights.

Jesús Alvarado Nieves (October 7, 1959 – April 28, 2017) was a Mexican luchador (professional wrestler). Alvarado worked under the name Brazo de Oro (Spanish for "Arm of gold"). Alvarado worked as a booker for Consejo Mundial de Lucha Libre (CMLL) and as head of the wrestlers' union. Brazo de Oro was part of the Alvarado wrestling family. Brazo de Oro's son La Mascara is a CMLL wrestler, as are his nephews Máximo and Psycho Clown. Additionally, Brazo de Oro was previously married to former CMLL World Women's Champion Lady Apache. Alvarado died on April 28, 2017 after suffering a heart attack in Mexico City at the age of 57.

Brenda Beers (born 1996) is a Dutch softball player. She is member of Olympia Haarlem and the Netherlands women's national softball team. With the national team she became European champion at the 2022 Women's Softball European Championship.

Brenden Dillon (born November 13, 1990) is a Canadian ice hockey defenceman. He currently plays for the Washington Capitals of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the Dallas Stars and San Jose Sharks. Before playing in the NHL, Dillon played one season with the Hope Icebreakers of the Pacific Junior Hockey League (PJHL) and four seasons with the Seattle Thunderbirds of the Western Hockey League (WHL). Dillon would go undrafted but was signed to a three-year entry-level contract with the Dallas Stars on March 1, 2011. On February 1, 2013, Dillon was able to score his first NHL goal and his first career Gordie Howe hat trick in a 4–3 shootout win against the Phoenix Coyotes. On November 21, 2014, the Stars traded Dillon to the San Jose Sharks in exchange for Jason Demers and a 2016 third-round pick.

Brendan Rodgers (born 26 January 1973) is the Celtic Football Manager and winner of the Scottish league 2023/2024. Formally a Northern Irish football manager and former player. He was the manager of Premier League club Leicester City. He managed Liverpool from 2012 to 2015, finishing second in the Premier League in 2014. He was sacked in October 2015. In 2016, he joined Scottish Premiership club Celtic. In his two-and-a-half seasons with Celtic, he won two domestic trebles. In 2019, he left Celtic to manage Leicester City. He has also managed Watford, Reading and Swansea City. In his playing days, he played for Ballymena United and Reading before retiring at the age of 20 due to injury. Rodgers was born in Carnlough. His son, Anton (born 1993), is a footballer.

Brenda Villa (born April 18, 1980) is an American water polo player and coach. Brenda Villa is a three time Olympic medalist in Water Polo. She was born in Commerce, California. She started playing Water Polo at age 8 at the Commerce Aquatorium. She was inspired to take up Water Polo by her brother Edgar. Edgar pushed her to become stronger and better. She was always looking for his approval. Another challenge was that she was playing against older kids who were mostly boys. There were not enough girls to make a team. Villa graduated from high school in 1998. She earned a college scholarship to Stanford for her skills in Water Polo. She was named the top collegiate player on the Stanford Women’s Water Polo team. Villa is famous for her accomplishments in Water Polo which have earned her several Olympic medals. Brenda started playing for the US National Team in 1998. She helped them qualify for the Olympics. She and her teammates appeared on CNBC, MSNBC, and NBC. In 2003, her team won the World Championship in Water Polo. Villa was also a big part in the Pan Am championships. Right now, she is working as the Water Polo Coach at Castilleja School in Palo Alto, California, USA. Villa is possibly going to be recognized in the Olympic Hall of Fame.

Sir Brendan Foster (born 12 January 1948) is a British former long-distance runner, athletics commentator and road race organiser. He founded the Great North Run, one of the sport's most high profile half-marathon races. Foster was born in Hebburn, South Tyneside. As an athlete, he won the bronze medal in the 10,000 metres at the 1976 Summer Olympics, and the gold medal in the 5,000 metres at the 1974 European Championships and the 10,000 metres at the 1978 Commonwealth Games.

Brenden Russell Aaronson (born October 22, 2000) is an American professional soccer player who plays as an attacking midfielder or winger for Union Berlin, on loan from side Leeds United, and the United States national team. After playing for different college teams he was selected to the Philadelphia Union's YSC Academy. He played in the team and completed his high school education. 2017-18 he played for Bethlehem Steel, the feeder team of Philadelphia Union. Then he went on to Philadelphia Union. On October 16, 2020, it was announced that Aaronson would join Red Bull Salzburg in January 2021 after the MLS season ended. He made his debut for Salzburg on January 25 and his first goal on February 10, 2021. After two seasons in Austria he went to Leeds United in the Premier League. 2023-24 he was loaned to Bundesliga club 1. FC Union Berlin in Germany for one season. He played in the US U15 and U23 team. His first match for the US national team was in a 1–0 win over Costa Rica. During his first call for the national team he did not play.
