Cláudio Brito (born 5 April 1965) is a retired handball player from Brazil. Cláudio competed at the 1992 Summer Olympics. He was born on 5 April 1965.

Clàudia Peña Hidalgo (born 26 October 2004) is a Spanish Rugby sevens and Rugby union player. She won a gold medal at the 2023 Rugby Europe Women's Championship. She competed at the 2023 Rugby World Cup. and 2024 Women's Women's Championship.

Cläre Voss (born about 1900s; fl. 1921-1927) was a German track and field athlete, competing in sprint events and the athletics triathlon. She was active during the 1920s, during the early era of women’s athletics in Germany. She was a member of Berliner SC and represented Germany at international competitions. In the 4 x 100 meters relay she was the world record holder. She was three times national champion. She won with the Berliner SC 4 x 100 meters relay team the bronze medal at the national championships in national champion in 1921, 1922 and 1923. The following three years, 1924, 1925 and 1926, she became with the team national champion and won again the bronze medal in 1927. She won two other bronze medals at the national championships in the athletics thriathlon in 1925 and 1927. Together with teammates Lilli Henoch, Charlotte Köhler and Gerda Pöting she set an official world record in the 4 × 100 meter relay in Köln on 11 July 1926 with a time of 50.3 seconds. She represented Germany internationaly, including at the 1926 Paris international women's athletics meeting. At this meeting she won with the German team the 4 x 100 metres relay event. According to some sources she also finished third in the 200 metres, however other sources stated it was Emmi Haux.

Jacobus "Co" Adriaanse (born 21 July 1947) is a Dutch football manager. As player he played as centre-back for De Volewijckers anf FC Utrecht. Adriaanse played six seasons with (now dissolved) De Volewijckers (1964 until 1970) and also six seasons with Utrecht (1970 until 1976). Adriaanse began his managing career with Zilvermeeuwen in 1979for four years and then went to AZ as scout and youth trainer. Then he coached PEC Zwolle and FC Den Haag for four seasons each. He then managed the youth side of Ajax, for five seasons. In 1997 he became manager of Willem II. The team finished in fifth place and had wins over Feyenoord (2–0) and defending champions PSV (4–1). The fifth place was the first qualification for European football since 1963. In the 1998–99 UEFA Cup they reached round 2 but lost to Betis Sevilla. After the team did not reach another European competition, Adriaans resigned in 2000. Adriaanse returned to Ajax as manager and reached a third place but was sacked early in the next season because of poor results. In November 2002 Adriaanse was signed to AZ. In the first season they finished tenth, in the next fifth. They qualified for the UEFA Cup 2004-05. There they reached the semi-finals but lost to Sporting Clube de Portugal. In the Eredivisiethey finished third. On 24 May 2005 Adriaanse was presented as the new manager of Portuguese club Porto. In the first season as Porto coach, he achieved the double for the first time since Jose Mourinho left the club. On 9 August 2006 Adriaanse resigned as manager of Porto. In December 2006 he became coach of FC Metalurh Donetsk. On 17 May 2007 he resigned as manager of Metalurh Donetsk. On 27 August 2007 Adriaanse became manager of Al-Sadd but resigned as coach on 28 January 2008. On 13 March 2008 Adriaanse signed with the Austrian champion Red Bull Salzburg. He left the club after the end of the season finishing with the team as champion. 2010 he became manager of the Qatar Olympic team. His Middle East stint, however, lasted only 14 months, as his contract was terminated by mutual consent in March 2011. On 20 June 2011 he was named manager. In his first official match with the club, Adriaanse won the Johan Cruyff Shield against his former team Ajax. In January 2012 the contract was dissolved by Twente. 2014-15 Adriaanse was technical advisor at Utrecht. At the end of the season he left. Primeira Liga's Manager of the Season: 2006

Cori "Coco" Gauff (born March 13, 2004) is an American professional tennis player. She turned professional in 2018 and won her first Grand Slam tournament at the 2023 US Open. She also won the 2025 French Open. Gauff's highest singles world ranking is No. 2 achieved in June 2024.

Cody Garrett Runnels Rhodes (né Runnels; born June 30, 1985) better known simply by his ring name Cody Rhodes, is an American professional wrestler and actor. He is currently signed to WWE, where he performs on the SmackDown brand. Rhodes co-founded All Elite Wrestling, where he served as an executive vice president and wrestler from 2019 to 2022. He is a three-time WWE Champion, as well as 2025 King of the Ring. Rhodes is nicknamed "The American Nightmare". The son of Dusty Rhodes and the half-brother of Dustin Rhodes, he is married to Brandi Rhodes. Rhodes started his wrestling career for World Wrestling Entertainment (WWE) in 2006, working there for the next ten years. During this time, he became a two-time Intercontinental Champion and a six-time tag team champion (three-time World Tag Team Champion and three-time WWE Tag Team Champion). From 2014–2016, he was known as Stardust. Rhodes was released from WWE in May 2016. After that he worked on the Independent circuit, for Ring of Honor (where he won the ROH World Championship, the ROH World Six-Man Tag Team Championship and the NWA World Heavyweight Championship, which was also won by his father), Total Nonstop Action Wrestling/Impact Wrestling and New Japan Pro-Wrestling (where he was an important member of the Bullet Club and a former IWGP United States Heavyweight Champion). On January 1, 2019, Rhodes joined the newly founded company All Elite Wrestling (AEW). There he was an executive vice president and a record-tying three-time TNT Champion (also being the first man to win the title). On February 15, 2022, he left AEW. That April he returned to WWE on the first night of WrestleMania 38, defeating Seth "Freakin" Rollins. He would go on to win the Undisputed WWE Tag Team Championship (his fourth Raw Tag Team Championship and his first SmackDown Tag Team Championship) and the Royal Rumble Match in 2023 and 2024, becoming the fourth wrestler to win that match twice in a row. On April 7, 2024, at night two of WrestleMania XL, Rhodes defeated Roman Reigns to win the Undisputed WWE Universal Championship. It was Rhodes' first world title in WWE and it also ended Reigns' record-setting 1,316-day reign. By winning, Rhodes also became a Triple Crown champion. Cody Eakin (born May 24, 1991) is a Canadian ice hockey centre. He plays in the National Hockey League (NHL). He has played for the Buffalo Sabres, Winnipeg Jets, Washington Capitals, Dallas Stars, and Vegas Golden Knights. Before playing in the NHL, Eakin played parts of 4 seasons with the Swift Current Broncos of the Western Hockey League (WHL). He was drafted 85th overall by the Washington Capitals in the 2009 NHL Entry Draft. He signed a three-year entry level contract with the Capitals on October 20, 2009. On November 1, 2011, Eakin was called up from the Hershey Bears. The same day, Eakin made his NHL debut in a 5-4 overtime win against the Anaheim Ducks. On November 4, 2011, Eakin scored his first NHL goal against Cam Ward of the Carolina Hurricanes. On June 22, 2012, the Capitals traded Eakin along with a second round pick to the Dallas Stars in exchange for Mike Ribeiro.

Cody Douglas Hodgson (born February 18, 1990) is a Canadian former professional ice hockey centre. He played parts of 6 seasons in the National Hockey League (NHL). He played for the Vancouver Canucks, Buffalo Sabres, and Nashville Predators. Hodgson is a one-time All-Star, being named one in 2012. Before playing in the NHL, Hodgson played four seasons with the Brampton Battalion of the Ontario Hockey League (OHL). He had a successful time during his time with the Battalion. On October 5, 2008, the Battalion named Hodgson as their new captain. In 2009, he was selected to play in the OHL All-Star Classic. In the game, he recorded five points and was named player of the game. The five-point game tied an OHL record for most points in an All-Star game. In the 2008–09 season, Hodgson had a very great season. He was named to the OHL First All-Star Team, and won both the William Hanley Trophy for being the OHL's most sportsmanlike player and the Red Tilson Trophy for being the OHL player of the year. In 2009, he was named the CHL Player of the Year. He helped the team during the playoffs, defeating the Peterborough Petes, Mississauga St. Michael's Majors, and Belleville Bulls. They were defeated in the Finals by the Windsor Spitfires four games to one to win the J. Ross Robertson Cup. He was selected 10th overall by the Vancouver Canucks in the 2008 NHL entry draft. On October 5, Hodgson signed a three-year, $2.625 million entry-level contract with the Canucks. On February 1, 2011, the Canucks called Hodgson up and he made his NHL debut in a 4–1 win against the Dallas Stars. The next day, on February 2, Hodgson scored his first NHL goal against Ilya Bryzgalov in a 6–0 win against the Phoenix Coyotes. He helped the team during the playoffs, defeating the Chicago Blackhawks, Nashville Predators, and San Jose Sharks. The Canucks were defeated in the Finals by the Boston Bruins four games to three. In 2012, he was selected for that year's 2012. On February 27, 2012, the Canucks traded Hodgson along with Alexander Sulzer to the Buffalo Sabres in exchange for Zack Kassian and Marc-André Gragnani. On September 11, 2013, Hodgson signed a six-year, $25.5 million contract to stay with the Sabres. He played parts of four seasons with the team. On July 1, 2015, Hodgson signed a one-year, $1.05 million contract to join the Nashville Predators. On January 13, 2016, the Predators waived Hodgson and he joined their Hockey League-affiliate Milwaukee Admirals. On October 3, Hodgson announced that he was retiring from playing professional ice hockey to work with the Predators and coach for their Little Preds Learn to Play Program. Hodgson later revealed that he had retired because he had diagnosed with malignant hyperthermia and it had caused him to struggle during his final seasons.

Cody Robert Simpson (born 11 January 1997) is an Australian singer, model, actor, and a former competitive swimmer. He has released four solo studio albums: Paradise (2012), Surfers Paradise (2013), Free (2015), and Cody Simpson (2022). He also played Dmitry in the Broadway musical Anastasia from November 2018 through April 2019. In 2022, Simpson joined the Australian Swim Team after qualifying for the Commonwealth Games during Australia's team trials. In June 2024, he retired from competitive swimming after failing to qualify for Paris Olympics.

Cody Ceci (born December 21, 1993) is a Canadian professional ice hockey defenceman. He currently plays for the Los Angeles Kings of the National Hockey League (NHL). Ceci has also played for the Ottawa Senators, Toronto Maple Leafs, Pittsburgh Penguins, Edmonton Oilers, San Jose Sharks, and Dallas Stars. Before playing in the NHL, Ceci played four seasons with the Ottawa 67's and one season with the Owen Sound Attack of the Ontario Hockey League (OHL). He had a successful time with his teams. He was named to back-to-back OHL Second All-Star Teams. He was drafted 15th overall by the Ottawa Senators in the 2012 NHL entry draft. On August 23, 2012, Ceci signed a three-year, $2.775 million entry-level contract to join the Senators. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Binghamton Senators. On December 12, 2013, Ottawa called him up and Ceci made his NHL debut in a 2–1 win against the Buffalo Sabres. On December 16, Ceci scored his first NHL goal and the overtime winner against Brian Elliott in a 3–2 overtime win against the St. Louis Blues. On August 23, 2016, Ceci signed a two-year, $5.6 million contract to stay with the Senators. On 3 August 2018, Ceci signed a one-year, $4,3 million contract to stay with the Senators. On July 1, 2019, the Senators traded Ceci along with Ben Harpur, Aaron Luchuk, and a 2020 third-round draft pick to the Toronto Maple Leafs in exchange for Connor Brown, Michael Carcone, and Nikita Zaitsev. On July 4, 2019, Ceci signed a one-year contract to stay with the Leafs. Ceci played one season with the Leafs. On October 17, 2020, Ceci signed a one-year, $1.25 million contract to join the Pittsburgh Penguins. He scored 4 goals and recorded 13 assists for 17 points in 53 regular season games for the Penguins. On July 28, 2021, Ceci signed a four-year, $13 million contract to join the Edmonton Oilers. He played three seasons with the Oilers. On August 18, 2024, the Oilers traded Ceci along with a 2025 third-round draft pick to the San Jose Sharks in exchange for Ty Emberson. He scored 4 goals and recorded 11 assists for 15 points in 54 regular season games for the Sharks. On February 1, 2025, the Sharks traded Ceci along with Mikael Granlund to the Dallas Stars in exchange for a 2025 first-round draft pick and a 2025 conditional third-round draft pick. He recorded 9 assists in 39 regular season games for the Stars. On July 1, 2025, Ceci signed a four-year, $18 million contract to join the Los Angeles Kings.

Cody Glass (born April 1, 1999) is a Canadian professional ice hockey forward. He currently plays for the New Jersey Devils of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the Vegas Golden Knights, Nashville Predators, and Pittsburgh Penguins. Before playing in the NHL, Glass played five seasons with the Portland Winterhawks of the Western Hockey League (WHL). He had a successful time with the Winterhawks. He won the Brad Hornung Trophy as the WHL's most sportsmanlike player and was named a West First Team All-Star three-straight times. He was drafted 6th overall by the Vegas Golden Knights of the 2017 NHL entry draft. He was the first player ever drafted by the Golden Knights. On July 15, 2017, Glass signed a three-year, $5.325 million entry-level contract to join the Knights. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Chicago Wolves. On October 2, 2019, the Knights called him up and Glass made his NHL debut in a 4–1 win against the San Jose Sharks. During the second period, he scored his first NHL goal against Martin Jones. On July 17, 2021, the Knights traded Glass to the Nashville Predators in exchange for Nolan Patrick. On March 2, 2024, he recorded his first NHL hat-trick in a 5–1 win against the Colorado Avalanche. On June 24, 2022, Glass signed a one-year contract to stay with the Predators. On June 24, 2022, Glass signed a two-year, $5 million contract to stay with the Predators. On August 13, 2024, the Predators traded Glass along with a 2025 third-round draft pick and a 2026 sixth-round draft pick to the Pittsburgh Penguins in exchange for Jordan Frasca. He scored four goals and recorded 11 assists in 51 regular season games for the Penguins. On March 7, 2025, the Penguins traded Glass along with Jonathan Gruden to the New Jersey Devils in exchange for Max Graham, Chase Stillman, and a 2027 third-round draft pick. On June 24, 2022, Glass signed a two-year, $5 million contract to stay with the Devils.

Colby Cave (December 26, 1994 – April 11, 2020) was a Canadian professional ice hockey centre. He played for the Boston Bruins and Edmonton Oilers of the National Hockey League (NHL). His career lasted from 2015 until his death in 2020. He was born in North Battleford, Saskatchewan, Canada. Cave had a brain bleed caused by a cyst on April 6–7, 2020. He had emergency surgery on April 7 in Toronto. He died while under a medically induced coma in the early hours of April 11, aged 25.

Colby Joseph Armstrong (born November 23, 1982) is a Canadian broadcaster and former professional ice hockey right winger. He played parts of 8 seasons in the National Hockey League (NHL). He played for the Pittsburgh Penguins, Atlanta Thrashers, Toronto Maple Leafs, and Montreal Canadiens. Outside of the NHL, Armstrong played for the Växjö Lakers of the Swedish Hockey League (SHL). He currently works as an analyst for both NHL on Sportsnet and SportsNet Pittsburgh for Penguins games. Before playing in the NHL, Armstrong played parts of four seasons with the Red Deer Rebels of the Western Hockey League (WHL). He had a successful time with the Rebels. During the playoffs, he helped the Rebels go on a run. They defeated the Lethbridge Hurricanes, Calgary Hitmen, and Swift Current Broncos. They went on to defeat the Portland Winterhawks to win the President's Cup and also the Scotty Munro Memorial Trophy for being the best regular season record. The Rebels earned a berth in the Memorial Cup tournament. Armstrong helped the Rebels defeat the Val-d'Or Foreurs in the final to win the first Memorial Cup in Rebels franchise history. Armstrong served as the Rebels captain. He was drafted 21st overall by the Pittsburgh Penguins in the 2001 NHL entry draft. On September 3, Armstrong signed an entry-level contract to join the Penguins. He was immediately sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Wilkes–Barre/Scranton Penguins. He played parts of four seasons with WBS. On August 12, 2005, Armstrong signed a contract to stay with the Penguins. On December 29, 2005, the Penguins called him up and Armstrong made his NHL debut in a 6–2 win against the New Jersey Devils. On January 3, 2006, he recorded his first NHL point, assisting on a Maxime Talbot goal in a 6–4 win against the Montreal Canadiens. Three days later on January 6, Armstrong scored his first NHL goal against Kari Lehtonen in a 6–3 loss against the Atlanta Thrashers. On July 21, Armstrong signed a one-year contract to stay with the Penguins. On February 26, 2008, the Penguins traded Armstrong along with Angelo Esposito, Erik Christensen and a 2008 first-round draft pick to the Atlanta Thrashers in exchange for Marián Hossa and Pascal Dupuis. On July 16, 2009, Armstrong signed a two-year, $2.4 million contract to stay with the Thrashers. On July 1, 2010, Armstrong signed a three-year, $9 million contract to join the Toronto Maple Leafs. His time was the Leafs was not very successful and he missed a lot of playing time because of injuries. On June 30, 2012, the Maple Leafs bought out the rest of Armstrong's contract. On July 1, 2012, Armstrong signed a one-year, $1 million contract to join the Montreal Canadiens. He scored 2 goals and recorded 3 assists for 5 points in 37 games for the Canadiens. After being injured in a game against the Carolina Hurricanes, Armstrong was ruled out for the rest of the season. It was the last time he played in the NHL. On July 27, 2013, Armstrong left the NHL and North America after signing a contract to join the Växjö Lakers of the Swedish Hockey League (SHL). He scored 12 goals and recorded 7 assists for 19 points in 37 games for the Lakers. He retired from playing professional ice hockey in 2014. Armstrong's younger brother Riley Armstrong was also a professional hockey player and played 2 games for the San Jose Sharks.

Colby David Bishop (born 4 November 1996) is a English professional footballer who plays as a forward for EFL Championship club Portsmouth. Bishop was born in Nottingham, Nottinghamshire. On 13 July 2019, Bishop joined Accrington Stanley of League One for an undisclosed fee. He made his debut for the club on the opening day of the season, playing the duration of a 2–0 defeat at Lincoln City, before he scored his first goal for the club in his second appearance, equalising from the penalty spot as Accrington were knocked out of the EFL Cup by Sunderland in an eventual 3–1 defeat. On 21 July 2022, Bishop signed for League One club Portsmouth for an undisclosed fee on a three-year contract, with an option to extend for a further year. At the end of the 2022–23 season, Bishop was named as Portsmouth's Player of the Season. Ahead of the 2024–25 season, a routine heart scan identified a potential risk to Bishop who would undergo immediate surgery to rectify the matter.

Colbert Michael Hamels (born December 27, 1983) is an American professional baseball pitcher for the Chicago Cubs of Major League Baseball (MLB). He previously played for the Philadelphia Phillies from 2006 to 2015, and the Texas Rangers from 2015 to 2018. The Phillies drafted him out of high school in the first round of the 2002 MLB Draft (17th), and he began his career in the Phillies minor league system.. He was the top pitcher in the Phillies' minor league system in 2006. In May 2006, Hamels made his major league debut for the Phillies. After securing a long-term spot as a member of the Phillies starting rotation in his rookie season, he made large strides in the 2007 Major League Baseball season and won the Phillies' top major league pitcher award. He was the top pitcher on the team entering the 2008 season, and during the Phillies' postseason run, during which they ultimately won the 2008 World Series over the Tampa Bay Rays, he won the World Series Most Valuable Player Award. After the 2008 season, Hamels signed a three-year contract with the Phillies. His statistics declined over the next two seasons, struggling through a tumultuous 2009 campaign and somewhat bouncing back in 2010, however still not approaching his 2008 numbers. Over the next few seasons, Hamels was joined by fellow All-Star pitchers including Roy Halladay, Cliff Lee, and Roy Oswalt and flourished with them, putting up some of his top career seasons before suffering from poor run support in 2013. With the decline of his aging teammates, the team missed the postseason for the next few years, but Hamels remained one of the Phillies' consistent stars. Hamels was traded to the Texas Rangers in 2015, and he subsequently sparked their run to the AL West title that season. He spent parts of four seasons with the Rangers, including an All-Star season in 2016, before being traded to the Cubs in 2018.

Cole Jermaine Palmer (also known as CP20) (born 6 May 2002) is an English footballer. He plays as an attacking midfielder or winger for Chelsea and the England national team. He is one of the best young players in Europe. Palmer started playing for Manchester City and made his first senior game in 2020. He helped them win the Premier League, FA Cup, and UEFA Champions League in 2023. He moved to Chelsea in 2023 for £40 million and was named the best player for Chelsea and the best young player in the Premier League for the 2023–24 season. Palmer has played for England's youth teams and won the 2023 Under-21 Championship. He started playing for the senior England team in the same year.

Cole Caufield (born January 2, 2001) is a Canadian-American professional ice hockey right winger. He currently plays for the Montreal Canadiens of the National Hockey League (NHL). Before playing in the NHL, Caufield played parts of 2 seasons with the USA Hockey National Team Development Program of the United States Hockey League (USHL) and 2 years with the Wisconsin Badgers of the National Collegiate Athletic Association (NCAA). With the USNTDP, Caufield set the all-time record for the most goals scored in a season with 72 goals. This broke the last record held by Phil Kessel. Caufield also had a very successful university career. He was named a back-to-back Big Ten Scoring Champion and was named to the Big Ten All-Freshman Team, the All-First Team, and the Big Ten Freshman of the Year. He was drafted 15th overall overall by the Montreal Canadiens in the 2019 NHL Entry Draft. On March 27, 2021, Caufield signed a three-year, entry-level contract with the Canadiens. On April 26, Caufield made his NHL debut in a 2-1 win against the Calgary Flames. May 1, he scored his first NHL goal in a 3-2 overtime win against the Ottawa Senators. In March 2022, Caufield was named as the NHL Rookie of the Month, leading all rookies with 7 goals and 15 points. On June 5, 2023, Caufield signed an eight-year, $62.8 million extension to stay with the Canadiens.

Cole Perfetti (born January 1, 2002) is a Canadian professional ice hockey centre. He currently plays for the Winnipeg Jets of the National Hockey League (NHL). Before playing in the NHL, Perfetti played parts of two seasons with the Saginaw Spirit of the Ontario Hockey League (OHL). He had a successful time with the Spirit. He was named to the OHL First All-Rookie Team. The next season was even more productive for Perfetti as he was named to the OHL Second All-Star Team, and was named both the Bobby Smith Trophy winner for being the OHL's Scholastic Player of the Year and was also the CHL Scholastic Player of the Year. He was drafted 10th overall by the Winnipeg Jets in the 2020 NHL entry draft. On November 10, 2020, he signed a three-year, entry-level contract to join the Jets. He was immediately sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Manitoba Moose. On October 13, 2021, the Jets called him up and Perfetti made his NHL debut in a 4–1 loss to the Anaheim Ducks. On January 18, 2022, Perfetti scored his first NHL goal against Vítek Vaněček in a 4–3 overtime loss against the Washington Capitals. He helped the Jets during the playoffs. They defeated the St. Louis Blues four games to three in the first round. Perfetti scored the game-tying goal with three seconds left in Game 7 to bring the game to overtime where Adam Lowry scored the series-clinching goal. Perfetti's goal was a new league record for the latest game-tying goal in a seventh game. The Jets went on to lose to the Dallas Stars four games to two in the second round.

Cole Tyler Koepke (born May 17, 1998) is an American professional ice hockey left winger. He currently plays for the Winnipeg Jets of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the Tampa Bay Lightning and Boston Bruins. Before playing in the NHL, Koepke played two seasons with the Sioux City Musketeers of the United States Hockey League (USHL) and three years with the Minnesota Duluth Bulldogs of the National Collegiate Hockey Conference (NCHC). He had a successful time with his teams. He helped the Bulldogs when they went on a run in the playoffs. They defeated the Bowling Green Falcons, Quinnipiac Bobcats, and Providence Friars. They went on to defeat the UMass Minutemen 3–0 in the Final to win the second of back-to-back National Championship. He was also named to the all-NCHC first-team and the All-American second-team. He was drafted 183rd overall by the Tampa Bay Lightning in the 2018 NHL entry draft. On April 13, 2021, Koepke signed a two-year entry-level contract to join the Lightning. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Syracuse Crunch. On October 17, 2015, the Lightning called him up and Koepke made his NHL debut in a 3–1 loss against the New York Rangers. On November 13, 2022, Koepke scored his first NHL goal against Charlie Lindgren in a 6–3 win against the Washington Capitals. On June 15, 2023, Koepke signed a one-year contract to stay with the Lightning. On July 1, 2024, Koepke signed a one-year contract to join the Boston Bruins. He played one season with the Bruins. He scored 10 goals and recorded 7 assists for 17 points in 73 regular season games for the team. On July 1, 2025, Koepke signed a one-year, $1 million contract to join the Winnipeg Jets.

Cole James O'Hara (born June 20, 2002) is a Canadian professional ice hockey right winger. He currently plays for the Milwaukee Admirals of the American Hockey League (AHL) and is a prospect for the Nashville Predators of the National Hockey League (NHL). Before playing in the NHL, O'Hara played parts of five seasons with the Tri-City Storm of the United States Hockey League (USHL) and years with the UMass Minutemen of Hockey East. He had a successful time with his teams. With the Minutemen, he was named to the All-Hockey East First Team and was also a AHCA East First Team All-American. He was drafted 114th overall by the Nashville Predators in the 2022 NHL entry draft. On October 16, 2020, O'Hara signed a two-year entry-level contract to join the Predators. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Milwaukee Admirals. On January 3, 2025, the Predators called him up and O'Hara made his NHL debut in a 4–5 loss against the Anaheim Ducks. During the first period, he recorded his first NHL point after he assisted on a Steven Stamkos goal.

Cole Smith (born October 28, 1995) is an American professional ice hockey left winger. He currently plays for the Vegas Golden Knights of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the Nashville Predators. Before playing in the NHL, Smith played two seasons with the Steinbach Pistons of the Manitoba Junior Hockey League (MJHL) and four years with the North Dakota Fighting Hawks of the National Collegiate Hockey Conference (NCHC). He was not drafted by an NHL team. On March 19, 2020, Smith signed a three-year entry-level contract to join the Predators. He was sent down to play for their ECHL-affiliate Florida Everblades. On January 14, 2021, the Predators called him up and Smith made his NHL debut in a 3–1 win against the Columbus Blue Jackets. On July 15, Smith signed a one-year, $750,000 contract to stay with the Predators. On July 14, 2022, he signed another one-year contract to stay with the Predators. On October 7, he recorded his first NHL point after assisting on a Eeli Tolvanen goal in a 4–1 win against the San Jose Sharks. On January 21, 2023, Smith scored his first NHL goal against Jonathan Quick in a 5–3 win against the Los Angeles Kings. On January 24, 2024, Smith signed a two-year, $2 million contract to stay with the Predators. On March 3, 2026, the Predators traded Smith to the Vegas Golden Knights in exchange for Christoffer Sedoff and a 2028 third-round draft pick.

Cole Reinhardt (born February 1, 2000) is a Canadian professional ice hockey left winger. He currently plays for the Florida Panthers of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the Ottawa Senators and Vegas Golden Knights. Before playing in the NHL, Reinhardt played four seasons with the Brandon Wheat Kings of the Western Hockey League (WHL). He was drafted 181st overall by the Ottawa Senators in the 2020 NHL entry draft. On September 13, 2012, Reinhardt signed an three-year, $1.97 million entry-level contract to join the Predators. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Belleville Senators. On April 7, 2022, Ottawa called him up and Reinhardt made his NHL debut in a 3–2 loss against the Nashville Predators. On November 25, he recorded his first NHL point after assisting on a Adam Gaudette goal in a 6–4 loss against the Vegas Golden Knights. On March 27, 2014, Reinhardt scored his first NHL goal against Dustin Wolf in a 4–3 win against the Calgary Flames. On June 14, 2024, Reinhardt signed a one-year, $775,000 contract to stay with the Senators. On July 1, 2025, Reinhardt signed a two-year, $812,500 contract to join the Vegas Golden Knights. He scored 3 goals and recorded 4 assists in 44 regular season games with the Knights. On March 5, 2026, the Knights placed Reinhardt onto waivers and his contract was picked up by the Florida Panthers the next day.

Cole Schwindt (born April 25, 2001) is a Canadian professional ice hockey forward. He currently plays for the Florida Panthers of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the Calgary Flames and Vegas Golden Knights. Before playing in the NHL, Schwindt played three seasons with the Mississauga Steelheads of the Ontario Hockey League (OHL). He was drafted 81st overall by the Florida Panthers of the 2019 NHL entry draft. On April 9, 2020, Schwindt signed a three-year entry-level contract to join the Panthers. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Syracuse Crunch and Charlotte Checkers. On December 16, 2021, the Panthers called him up and Schwindt made his NHL debut in a 4–1 loss against the Los Angeles Kings. On July 22, 2022, the Panthers traded Schwindt along with Jonathan Huberdeau, MacKenzie Weegar, and a 2025 conditional first-round draft pick to the Calgary Flames in exchange for Matthew Tkachuk and a 2025 conditional fourth-round draft pick. He played four regular season games for the Flames. On October 6, 2024, the Flames placed Schwindt onto waivers and his contract was picked up by the Vegas Golden Knights the next day. On October 11, he recorded his first NHL point after assisting on a Shea Theodore goal in a 4–3 win against the St. Louis Blues. On April 16, 2025, Schwindt scored his first NHL goal on an empty-net in a 4–1 win against the Vancouver Canucks. On July 6, 2025, Schwindt signed a one-year contract to stay with the Knights. On October 3, 2025, the Knights placed Schwindt back onto waivers and his contract was picked up by the Florida Panthers the next day.

Colin Matthew Delaney (born September 7, 1986) is an American professional wrestler. He is best known for his time with WWE on its ECW brand. He has also wrestled for All Elite Wrestling (AEW) and for many independent promotions. These include Squared Circle Wrestling, Chikara, NWA Upstate, Combat Zone Wrestling and the International Wrestling Cartel. He has wrestled using the ring names Colin Olsen and the "Extremely Cute Wrestler" Colin Delaney. Delaney made his World Wrestling Entertainment debut as a jobber, seen wrestling on the ECW show. On August 15, Delaney was released by WWE. Colin has an older brother Ed who competes as "Hangin' Tough" Freddie Midnight, and younger brother Brian who competed as Mr. Bodacious. AIW Tag Team Championship (6 times) – with Jimmy Olsen (1) and Cheech (5) IWC Tag Team Championship (1 time) – with Keith Haught NWA Empire Heavyweight Championship (1 time) NWA Empire Tag Team Championship (1 time) – with Mean Marcos NWA Empire Lord of the Dance Championship (1 time) NWA Southern Junior Heavyweight Championship (1 time) NWA Upstate Tag Team Championship (1 time) – with Jimmy Olsen PWI ranked #262 of the top 500 singles wrestlers in the PWI 500 in 2015 RCW Tag Team Championship (1 time) – with Jimmy Olsen 2CW Tag Team Championship (1 time) – with Jimmy Olsen STW Tag Team Championship (1 time) - with Cheech UPW Tag Team Championship (1 time) - with Cheech Upstate 8 Tournament (2018) - with Cheech Xcite Tag Team Championship (1 time) - with Cheech
Colin Bell (26 February 1946 – 5 January 2021) was an English footballer. He played for England national team. Bell was diagnosed with bowel cancer in 2005. He died on 5 January 2021, aged 74.

Colin Collindridge (15 November 1920 – 14 April 2019) was an English footballer. He played as both an outside left and a centre forward. The early part of his playing career happened during World War II. He later played for clubs Sheffield United, Nottingham Forest and Coventry City in the Football League. Collindridge was born in Barnsley, Yorkshire. He died in 2019, at the age of 98.

Colin Zachary Allred (born April 15, 1983) is an American politician and civil rights attorney. He used to be a professional football player. He is a Democrat. He was the U.S. Representative for from 2019 to 2025. That district covers the northeastern corner of Dallas. It also has many of its northeastern suburbs such as Garland, Richardson, University Park, Highland Park and Rowlett. When he was a football player, he was a linebacker who played for the Tennessee Titans in the National Football League (NFL). Allred stopped playing football to go back to law school for a Juris Doctor degree, from the University of California, Berkeley. He then worked in the Obama administration and the U.S. Attorney's office. Allred unsuccessfully ran for the U.S. Senate in 2024 against incumbent Republican Senator Ted Cruz. He ran for the U.S. Senate again in 2026, however dropped out before the primaries to successfully run against U.S. Representative Julie Johnson in the 33rd congressional district. Allred went to Hillcrest High School in Dallas, and then to Baylor University. He played college football at Baylor; he was a linebacker. In December 2005, Allred graduated from Baylor with a B.A. degree in history. Allred joined the Tennessee Titans after the 2006 NFL Draft on May 4, 2006. After his football career, Allred went to law school. He graduated from UC Berkeley School of Law in 2014. Then, Allred was a special assistant in the Department of Housing and Urban Development's Office of General Counsel. After that, Allred worked as a lawyer at the Perkins Coie law firm, where he worked on voting rights cases. He also served as the lawyer for different political candidates and advocacy groups. Politico, a political news source, described him as a "civil rights attorney." On April 21, 2017, Allred said he would challenge the current Representative from his district, Republican Pete Sessions, in the 2018 election. Allred won the most votes in the Democratic primary, but did not get more than 50 percent; he won by 20 points. Two of the other candidates also used to work in the Obama administration. In the May 22 runoff election, Allred beat Lewisville businesswoman Lillian Salerno, receiving 69.5% of the vote. Allred then competed with Sessions for the 32nd District seat. As of the November 2016 election, the seat was considered a "swing district" because Democratic presidential candidate Hillary Clinton received marginally more votes than Donald Trump even as Sessions, a Republican, was reelected with no major-party opposition. Allred has described himself as a moderate Democrat. On November 6, 2018, Allred was elected to the United States House of Representatives for the 32nd district of Texas. Allred's victory was considered an upset because Sessions has been in Congress since 1997 and has represented the 32nd District since 2003. Allred became the second person to represent this district since it was created in 2003, and the first Democrat. Sessions used to represent the nearby 5th District, but had switched after the district maps were changed. In February 2019, Allred endorsed Julian Castro in the 2020 presidential race. Castro, like Allred, is from Texas. Castro used to be the Housing and Urban Development Secretary. Allred was elected in November 2018 as co-president of the 116th Congressional Freshman Class. The other president was Representative Haley Stevens of Michigan. Subcommittee on the Middle East, North Africa and International Terrorism Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure Subcommittee on Railroads, Pipelines, and Hazardous Materials Subcommittee on Disability Assistance and Memorial Affairs On May 3, 2023, Allred announced his candidacy for the United States Senate in 2024, running against Republican incumbent Ted Cruz. On March 5, 2024, Allred won the primary nomination for the Democratic Party. He lost the election to Cruz in November 2024 by 8.6 points. On July 1, 2025, Allred announced his candidacy for the United States again, this time running against Republican Senator John Cornyn in the 2026 election. On December 8, 2025 Allred announced he was ending his campaign, to instead run in Texas's 33rd congressional district, following Representative Jasmine Crockett's entry into the Democratic race. Allred married Alexandra Eber on March 25, 2017. Their son, Jordan, was born on February 12, 2019.

Colin Clark (April 11, 1984 – August 26, 2019) was an American soccer player. He was born in Fort Collins, Colorado. Clark played for men's national soccer team in 2009. From 2006 through 2010, he played for the Colorado Rapids and for the Houston Dynamo from 2010 through 2012. On August 26, 2019, Clark died after suffering a heart attack; he was 35 years old.
