Clark (born 1931), Canadian mathematician and behavioural ecologist

Colin Grainger (10 June 1933 – 20 June 2022) was an English footballer. He played outside left and had a 16-year career in the Football League from 1950 to 1966. He made seven appearances for the England national football team between 1956 until 1957. He was born in Havercroft, West Yorkshire, England. Grainger played for Sunderland A.F.C. between 1957 until 1960, making 120 appearances. From 1953 until 1957, he played Sheffield United F.C., making 88 appearances. He also played for Port Vale F.C. and Doncaster Rovers F.C.. In March 2020, Grainger was moved to a care home in Kirklees, West Yorkshire. He died on 20 June 2022, ten days after his 89th birthday. Yorkshire League Division 2 promotion: 1972–73

Colin Blackwell (born March 28, 1993) is an American professional ice hockey center. He currently plays for the Dallas Stars of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the Nashville Predators, New York Rangers, Seattle Kraken, Toronto Maple Leafs, and Chicago Blackhawks. Before playing in the NHL, Blackwell played parts of 4 years with the Harvard Crimson of the National Collegiate Athletic Association (NCAA). He helped the Crimson win the ECAC Tournament Championship. He was drafted 194th overall by the San Jose Sharks in the 2011 NHL Entry Draft. He only played for their AHL-affiliate San Jose Barracuda. On November 2, 2017, Blackwell signed a contract with the Rochester Americans. On July 3, 2018, Blackwell signed a two-year, two-way contract with the Nashville Predators. On January 19, 2019, Blackwell made his NHL debut in a 4-2 loss against the Florida Panthers. On December 23, Blackwell recorded his first point in the NHL, assisting on a Roman Josi goal in a 3-2 win against the Arizona Coyotes. On January 9, 2020, Blackwell scored his first NHL goal in a 5-2 win against the Chicago Blackhawks. On October 9, 2020, Blackwell signed a $725,000; two-year contract with the New York Rangers. During the 2021 NHL Expansion Draft, the newly formed Seattle Kraken selected Blackwell. He played 39 games with them. On March 20, 2022, the Kraken traded Blackwell along with Mark Giordano to the Toronto Maple Leafs in exchange for a second and third-round pick. Blackwell scored one goal and two points in the playoffs during the First Round but the Leafs eventually lost to the Tampa Bay Lightning. On July 13, Blackwell signed a two-year, $2.4 million contract with the Chicago Blackhawks. The Blackhawks named Blackwell as their nominee for the Bill Masterton Memorial Trophy. On July 2, 2024, Blackwell signed a one-year, $775,000 contract with the Dallas Stars.

Colin Addison (18 May 1940 – 31 October 2025) was an English professional footballer and manager. He started his career by playing with York City before moving to Nottingham Forest, Arsenal and Sheffield United. His managerial career started with Hereford United in 1971. Addison died in Hereford, England on 31 October 2025 at the age of 85.

Colin Lloyd (born 7 August 1973 in Colchester, Essex), nicknamed "Jaws", is an English professional darts player. He is a player on the Professional Darts Corporation circuit. He used to be a world champion and he has won two major titles in the PDC. He appeared in the Dartsworld in 1999. In 2000, he had his first time on television. In 2002, he recorded his first major success when he lost in the semi-finals of the PDC World Championships against Peter Manley. In 2003 he reached the semifinals of the Las Vegas Desert Classics, 2004, he won the Sky Bet World Grand Prix 2005, the World Matchplay in Blackpool. In 2005 he was pitted against Phil Taylor in the finale. From 2004/2005 until the beginning of 2006 he was the No. 1 ranked player in the PDC.

Sir Colin Earl Meads (3 June 1936 – 20 August 2017) was a New Zealand rugby union player, coach and manager. He was born in Cambridge, New Zealand. He played 55 test matches (133 total games), most frequently in the lock forward position, for New Zealand's national team, the All Blacks, from 1957 until 1971. Nicknamed 'Pinetree', he was an icon within New Zealand rugby, and was named the country's Player of the Century at the NZRFU Awards in 1999. Meads died on 20 August 2017 in Te Kuiti, New Zealand of pancreatic cancer at the age of 81.

Colin Fyfe Miller (born 4 October 1964) is a Scottish-born Canadian professional soccer coach. He captained the Canadian national team several times while earning 61 caps (scoring 5 goals) in total. Scores and results list Canada's goal tally first.

Colin Sylvia (8 November 1985 – 28 October 2018) was an Australian rules footballer. He played for the Melbourne Football Club and Fremantle Football Club in the Australian Football League (AFL). Sylvia was born in Mildura, Victoria. Sylvia was killed in a car crash near Mildura on 28 October 2018 at the age of 32.

Colin Campbell McDonald (17 November 1928 – 11 January 2021) was an Australian cricketer. He played in 47 Test matches for his country from 1952 to 1961. He also played in 192 first-class matches between 1947 and 1963. McDonald was born in Glen Iris, Victoria. McDonald died in Melbourne, Victoria, on 11 January 2021. He was 92.

Colin Stuart (born July 8, 1982) is an American former professional ice hockey left winger. He played parts of 5 seasons in the National Hockey League (NHL). He played for the Atlanta Thrashers and Buffalo Sabres. Outside of the NHL, Stuart played for the Iserlohn Roosters of the Deutsche Eishockey Liga (DEL) and the Malmö Redhawks of the HockeyAllsvenskan. Before playing in the NHL, Stuart played parts of one season with the Lincoln Stars of the United States Hockey League (USHL) and four years with the Colorado College Tigers of the Western Collegiate Hockey Association (WCHA). He was drafted 135th overall by the Atlanta Thrashers in the 2001 NHL entry draft. On June 18, 2004, Stuart signed his entry-level contract to join the Thrashers. He was immediately sent down to play for both their AHL-affiliate Chicago Wolves and ECHL-affiliate Gwinnett Gladiators. On July 13, 2006, Stuart signed a contract extension to stay with the Thrashers. On December 29, 2007, the Thrashers called him up and Stuart made his NHL debut in a 5–0 win against the Boston Bruins. During the game, Stuart also recorded his first NHL point, assisting on a Pascal Dupuis goal. Two days later on December 31, Stuart scored his first NHL goal against Tim Thomas in a 5–2 loss against the Boston Bruins. On July 1, 2009, the Thrashers traded Stuart along with Garnet Exelby to the Toronto Maple Leafs in exchange for Pavel Kubina and Tim Stapleton. He never played a game with the Leafs. On July 27, the Leafs traded Stuart along with Anton Strålman and a 2012 seventh-round draft pick to the Calgary Flames in exchange for Wayne Primeau and a 2011 second-round draft pick. He was immediately sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Abbotsford Heat. On July 7, 2011, Stuart signed a one-year contract to play for the Buffalo Sabres. He played three games and then was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Rochester Americans. On September 18, 2012, Stuart decided to leave North America and sign a one-year contract to join the Iserlohn Roosters of the Deutsche Eishockey Liga (DEL). He scored 9 goals and recorded 12 assists for 21 points in 45 games for the Roosters. On July 25, 2013, Stuart returned to North America after he signed a one-year, two-way contract with the Vancouver Canucks. He was immediately sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Utica Comets. He scored 17 goals and recorded 8 assists for 25 points in 54 games for the Comets. On August 14, 2014, Stuart returned to Europe after signing a one-year contract to join the Malmö Redhawks of the HockeyAllsvenskan. On August 30, 2015, Stuart announced that he was retiring from playing professional ice hockey. Stuart's father Michael is a Mayo Clinic physician. His older brother Mike and younger brother Mark also played professional ice hockey in the NHL.

Colin Miller (born October 29, 1992) is a Canadian professional ice hockey defenceman. He currently plays for the Winnipeg Jets of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the Boston Bruins, Vegas Golden Knights, Buffalo Sabres, Dallas Stars, and New Jersey Devils. Before playing in the NHL, Miller played three seasons with the Sault Ste. Marie Greyhounds of the Ontario Hockey League (OHL). He was drafted 99th overall by the Buffalo Sabres in the 2017 NHL entry draft. On July 29, 2013, Miller signed a three-year, $1.80 million entry-level contract to join the Kings. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Manchester Monarchs. He never ended up playing a game for the Kings. On June 26, 2015, the Kings traded Miller along with Martin Jones and a 2015 first-round draft pick to the Boston Bruins in exchange for Milan Lucic. On October 10, 2015, Miller made his NHL debut in a 4–2 loss against the Montreal Canadiens. On October 14, he recorded his first NHL point, assisting on a Jimmy Hayes goal in a 6–2 win against the Colorado Avalanche. On November 3, Miller scored his first NHL goal against Kari Lehtonen in a 5–3 loss against the Dallas Stars. On July 14, 2016, Miller signed a two-year, $2 million contract to stay with the Bruins. On June 21, 2017, the Bruins left Miller unprotected in the 2017 NHL expansion draft and he was drafted by the Vegas Golden Knights. On July 7, 2018, Miller signed a four-year, $15.5 million contract the stay with the Knights. He played parts of two seasons with the Knights. On June 28, 2019, the Knights traded Miller to the Buffalo Sabres in exchange for a 2021 second-round draft pick and a 2022 fifth-round draft pick. He played three seasons with the Sabres. On July 13, 2022, Miller signed a two-year, $3.7 million contract to join with the Dallas Stars. he scored 6 goals and recorded 15 points for 21 points in 79 regular season games and recorded 1 assist in 10 playoff games. On July 1, 2023, the Stars traded Miller to the New Jersey Devils in exchange for a 2025 fifth-round draft pick. He scored 4 goals and recorded 4 assists for 8 points in 41 regular season games for the Devils. On March 8, 2024, the Devils traded Miller to the Winnipeg Jets in exchange for a 2026 fourth-round draft pick. On July 1, Miller signed a two-year, $3 million contract to stay with the Jets.

Collin Graf (born September 21, 2002) is an American professional ice hockey right winger. He currently plays for the San Jose Sharks of the National Hockey League (NHL). Before playing in the NHL, Graf played one year with the Union Garnet Chargers and two years with the Quinnipiac Bobcats of ECAC Hockey. He had a successful time with his teams. He was named the ECAC Hockey Player of the Year, was named both a AHCA East First and Second Team All-American, and was named to back-to-back All-ECAC First Teams. He was not drafted by an NHL team. On April 4, 2024, Graf signed a three-year, $941,667 entry-level contract to join the San Jose Sharks of the National Hockey League (NHL). On March 16, 2013, Graf made his NHL debut in a 3–2 overtime win against the St. Louis Blues. The next day, he recorded his first NHL point, assisting on a Luke Kunin goal in a 5–2 loss against the Arizona Coyotes. On March 18, Graf scored his first NHL goal against Sam Montembeault in a 4–3 loss against the Montreal Canadiens.

Scott Colton (born May 6, 1980) is an American professional wrestler. He currently wrestles for All Elite Wrestling (AEW) and competes under the ring name Colt Cabana. He also wrestles for their sister promotion Ring of Honor (ROH). He has also spent time wrestling in Wrestling Society X, World Wrestling Entertainment (WWE), Pro Wrestling Guerrilla (PWG), Chikara, and New Japan Pro-Wrestling (NJPW). During the Buy-In for Revolution, Cabana would make his debut in All Elite Wrestling (AEW). He would save SoCal Uncensored from a beatdown by The Dark Order. On March 1, 2020, it was announced that Cabana had signed a contract with the company. Cabana would make his AEW in-ring debut on the March 3 episode of Dynamite. He would team with SCU and they would defeat Dark Order. Cabana would enter the tournament to crown the first AEW TNT Champion. Cabana would lose in the first round to Lance Archer on the March 15 episode of Dynamite. At Double or Nothing, Cabana would compete in the Casino Ladder Match to try and earn a future match for the AEW World Championship but the match would be won by Brian Cage. The following Dynamite, Cabana would compete in a battle royal to determine who would become the number one contender for the AEW TNT Championship. The match would be won by Jungle Boy. On the June 3 and 10 episodes of Dynamite, Cabana would suffer losses to Chris Jericho and Sammy Guevara. After seeing his losing streak, Cabana would be approached by Mr. Brodie Lee and he would try and get Cabana to join his Dark Order stable. Cabana would then start teaming with Dark Order before officially joining them. On the November 2, 2022 episode of Dynamite, Cabana would challenge Chris Jericho for the ROH World Championship but would be defeated.

Colten Sopp (born May 18, 1991) is an American professional wrestler. He currently wrestles for All Elite Wrestling (AEW) and competes under the ring name Colten Gunn and is one third of the current Unified World Trios Champions. He wrestles in a tag team called The Gunns with his real-life younger brother Austin. His father is professional wrestler Billy Gunn, who also wrestles in All Elite Wrestling. During his time in AEW, Gunn has been a one-time AEW World Tag Team Champion and Unified World Trios Champion. On the November 17, 2020 episode of Dark, Gunn would make his in-ring debut for All Elite Wrestling (AEW). He would join his father Billy Gunn and his brother Austin as The Gunn Club. They would defeat BSHP King, Joey O’Riley, and Sean Maluta. On the February 11, 2022 episode of Rampage, Colten and Austin would face Jurassic Express (Jungle Boy and Luchasaurus) for the AEW World Tag Team Championships but lost. On February 8, 2023 episode of Dynamite, The Gunn's would defeat The Acclaimed (Max Caster and Anthony Bowens) to win the AEW World Tag Team Championships. This was Austin's first championship in AEW. They would lose the titles to FTR (Dax Harwood and Cash Wheeler) on the April 5 episode of Dynamite in a Title vs. Career match.

Colton Wyatt Parayko (born May 12, 1993) is a Canadian professional ice hockey defenceman. He currently plays for St. Louis Blues of the National Hockey League (NHL) and serves as their alternate captain. Parayko is a one-time Stanley Cup champion, winning with the Blues in 2019. Internationally, he plays for Canada and won the 4 Nations Face-Off with them in 2925. Before playing in the NHL, Parayko played three years with the Alaska Nanooks of the Central Collegiate Hockey Association (CCHA) and Western Collegiate Hockey Association (WCHA). He had a successful time with the Nanooks. In 2013, the team named him as the alternate captain. On September 24, 2014, the Nanooks upgraded Parayko and named him as their new captain. He was drafted 86th overall by the St. Louis Blues in the 2012 NHL entry draft. On March 10, 2015, Parayko signed a two-year entry-level contract to join the Blues. He was immediately sent down to the Blues AHL-affiliate Chicago Wolves. On October 8, the Blues called Parayko up to the team and he made his NHL debut in a 3–1 win against the Edmonton Oilers. Six days later, on October 14, he scored his first NHL goal against Jonas Hiller, a powerplay goal in the second period with his second career goal coming right after in a 4–3 win against the Calgary Flames. Despite suffering injuries which kept out of action, he still had a great 2015–16 season and was named to the NHL All-Rookie Team. He helped the Blues during the playoffs, defeating the Chicago Blackhawks and Dallas Stars. They were defeated by the San Jose Sharks four games to two in the Western Conference final. On June 20, 2017, Parayko signed a five-year, $27.5 million contract to stay with the Blues. He helped the Blues during the playoffs, defeating the Winnipeg Jets, Dallas Stars, and San Jose Sharks. In the Finals, they defeated by the Boston Bruins four games to three to win the first Stanley Cup in franchise history. On September 1, 2021, Parayko signed an eight-year, $52 million contract to stay with the Blues.

Colton Dach (born January 4, 2003) is a Canadian professional ice hockey centre. He currently plays for the Chicago Blackhawks of the National Hockey League (NHL). Before playing in the NHL, Dach played parts of two seasons with Saskatoon Blades, two seasons with the Kelowna Rockets, one season with the Seattle Thunderbirds of the Western Hockey League (WHL). He had a successful time with the Thunderbirds, helping them defeat the Winnipeg Ice four games to one in the final to win the Ed Chynoweth Cup. He was drafted 62nd overall by the Chicago Blackhawks in the 2021 NHL entry draft. On October 1, 2021, Dach signed a three-year, entry-level contract to join the Blackhawks. He was immediately sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Rockford IceHogs]]. On January 3, 2025, the Blackhawks called him up and he made his NHL debut in a 4–2 win against the Montreal Canadiens. On January 8, he recorded his first NHL point, assisting on a Frank Nazar goal in a 3–1 win against the Colorado Avalanche. On January 24, Dach scored his first NHL goal against Jonas Johansson in a 4–3 overtime loss against the Tampa Bay Lightning. Dach's older brother Kirby is also a professional ice hockey player and plays for the Montreal Canadiens.

Colton Sissons (born November 5, 1993) is a Canadian professional ice hockey defenceman. He currently plays for the Vegas Golden Knights of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the Boston Bruins, Seattle Kraken, and Nashville Predators. Before playing in the NHL, Sissons played one season with the Westside Warriors of the British Columbia Hockey League (BCHL) and three seasons with the Kelowna Rockets of the Western Hockey League (WHL). He was drafted 50th overall by the Nashville Predators in the 2012 NHL entry draft. On September 13, 2012, Sissons signed an three-year, $1.97 million entry-level contract to join the Predators. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Milwaukee Admirals. On January 28, 2014, the Predators called him up and Sissons made his NHL debut in a 4–3 win against the Winnipeg Jets. During the second period, he recorded his first NHL point after assisting on a Nick Spaling goal. On March 27, 2014, Sissons scored his first NHL goal against Matt Hackett in a 4–1 win against the Vegas Golden Knights. On February 22, 2016, Sissons signed a three-year, $1.875 million contract to stay with the Predators. On January 5, 2017, he recorded his first NHL hat-trick in a 6–1 win against the Tampa Bay Lightning. On July 23, 2019, Sissons signed a seven-year, $20 million contract to stay with the Predators. On June 30, 2025, the Predators traded Colton Sissons along with Jérémy Lauzon to the Vegas Golden Knights in exchange for Nicolas Hague and a 2027 conditional third-round draft pick. He scored 6 goals and recorded 5 assists in 66 regular season games with the Knights. On July 1, 2026, Sissons signed a two-year, $8.5 million contract to join with the Toronto Maple Leafs.

Colton White (born May 3, 1997) is a Canadian professional ice hockey centre. He currently plays for the Columbus Blue Jackets of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the New Jersey Devils and Anaheim Ducks. Before playing in the NHL, White played four seasons with the Sault Ste. Marie Greyhounds of the Ontario Hockey League (OHL). He was drafted 97th overall by the New Jersey Devils of the 2015 NHL entry draft. On September 21, 2016, White signed a three-year, $2.775 million entry-level contract to join the Devils. He was sent down to play for their AHL and ECHL-affiliate Binghamton Devils and Adirondack Thunder. On March 13, 2019, New Jersey called him up and White made his NHL debut in a 6–3 win against the Edmonton Oilers. On October 29, 2020, White signed a one-year contract to stay with the Devils. On July 14, 2021, White signed a one-year contract to stay with the Devils. On October 19, he recorded his first NHL point after assisting on a Jimmy Vesey goal in a 4–2 win against the Seattle Kraken. On July 14, 2022, White signed a two-year contract to join the Anaheim Ducks. He recorded six assists in 46 regular season games with the Ducks. On July 1, 2024, White signed a two-year contract to rejoin the New Jersey Devils. On October 6, the Devils placed White onto waivers and he was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Utica Comets. He recorded four assists in 23 regular season games in his return with the Devils. On July 6, 2026, White signed a two-year contract to join the Columbus Blue Jackets.

The Columbus Crew (known from 2015 to 2021 as Columbus Crew SC, and briefly in 2021 as Columbus SC) are an American soccer team that plays in Major League Soccer in Columbus, Ohio. They started play in 1996, playing at Ohio Stadium on the campus of Ohio State University until opening the new Columbus Crew Stadium in 1999. That stadium would be renamed Mapfre Stadium in 2015 and Historic Crew Stadium in late 2020. The Crew played their first match at the new Lower.com Field, now known as ScottsMiracle-Gro Field, on July 3, 2021. Shortly after the start of the 2021 season, the team announced a name change to Columbus SC. Fan reaction was extremely negative. On May 17, 2021, only a week after the change to Columbus SC, the team announced that it would return to the original name of Columbus Crew, without the "SC". MLS Cup (league championship): 2 (2008, 2020) MLS Supporters' Shield (best regular-season record): 3 (2004, 2008, 2009)

Commins Menapi (18 September 1977 – 18 November 2017) was a Solomon Islands striker. He was last the manager of Western United. He guided them to their first and only Telekom S league title season 2014/2015. In the 2006–2007 season, he became the first player to be sent off in a New Zealand Football Championship Grand Final. He represented the Solomon Islands national football team on over 30 occasions, scoring a record 34 goals (including 7 against non-FIFA members). Menapi was arguably the most famous Solomon Islands footballer. Menapi died in Honiara on 18 November 2017 of a heart attack at the age of 40.

Comunardo Niccolai (; 15 December 1946 – about 2 July 2024) was an Italian footballer, who played as a defender. He has played for Italy's national team. A tough, physically strong centre-back, Niccolai initially began his career with Torres in 1963, before joining Cagliari Calcio, where he played from 1964 to 1976, winning the only Serie A championship in the club's entire club history in 1970. He ended his career in 1977 with Perugia. Niccolai played 218 Serie A matches, and is still remembered today for his proneness to score own goals, including some very spectacular ones. His death was announced on 2 July 2024, at the age of 77.

Concepcion Hernandez Diaz (born October 13, 1972 in Murcia) is a goalball player from Spain. She is blind and is a B2 type goalball player. She played goalball at the 1996 Summer Paralympics. Her team was third. She played goalball at the 2000 Summer Paralympics. Her team was second.

Concepción Dueso Garcés (born October 27, 1967 in Huesca) is a goalball player from Spain. She is blind and is a type B3 goalball player. She played goalball at the 2000 Summer Paralympics. Her team was second.

Con de Wet de Lange (11 February 1981 – 18 April 2019) was a South African-born Scottish cricketer. He was a left-arm orthodox spin all-rounder and a right-handed batsman. He played for teams in South Africa before playing for Northamptonshire in England. Although he was born in Bellville, in what is now Western Cape, South Africa, he played for the Scotland national team. For a time, he was Scotland's vice-captain. In June 2015, he played his first game for Scotland against Afghanistan. He played his last game for Scotland in November 2017 against Papua New Guinea. In October 2018, Cricket Scotland said publicly that de Lange had brain cancer. He died on 18 April 2019, at the age of 38.
Francis Conn Findlay (April 24, 1930April 8, 2021) was an American Olympic rower and sailor. He won four Olympic medals in those two sports, including two golds in coxed pair.

Cornelius Dennis "Mad Dog" Madigan (October 4, 1934 – January 2, 2024) was a Canadian professional ice hockey defenceman notable for being the oldest rookie in National Hockey League history. After playing several years in senior leagues in Ontario and British Columbia in the late 1950s, Madigan had a long career as a minor league star, most notably with the Fort Wayne Komets of the International Hockey League for three seasons in the early 1960s, and then for the Portland Buckaroos of the Western Hockey League for nine seasons. He won accolades as First Team league All-Star in 1960, 1966, 1967, 1968 and 1969, Second Team All-Star in 1965, 1971 and 1972, as well as winning best defenceman honors in 1966. In the 1972–73 NHL season, the St. Louis Blues of the NHL bought Madigan's rights from the Buckaroos, and he joined the Blues in January 1973 at the age of 38, becoming the oldest rookie ever. He played for the Blues in twenty regular-season games and five playoff games, before finishing his career with Portland in parts of the two successive seasons. At the time of his retirement, Madigan was second in minor league history in career penalty minutes, and is still 62nd in that category. In addition to Madigan's hockey career, he had a minor role in the 1977 cult classic movie Slap Shot as legendary hockey goon Ross "Mad Dog" Madison. Madigan died on January 2, 2024.

Thomas Connell "Connie" Broden (April 6, 1932 – November 23, 2013) was a Canadian ice hockey forward. He played his whole National Hockey League career with the Montreal Canadiens. He two Stanley Cups with Montreal in 1957 and 1958. He was born in Montreal, Quebec. Broden died on November 23, 2013 at the St. Michael's Hospital in Toronto, Ontario. He was 81 years old. He was outlived by his wife and children.

Conrado Eugenio Marrero Ramos (April 25, 1911 – April 23, 2014), nicknamed "Connie," was a former Cuban professional baseball pitcher. Marrero played for the Washington Senators from 1950 to 1954. At age 102, Marrero was the oldest living former Major League Baseball player at the time of his death. He was born in Sagua la Grande, Cuba. Marrero died in Havana, Cuba from natural causes, aged 102.

Joseph Conrad Etienne Dion (11 August 1918 – 7 November 2014) was a Canadian professional ice hockey goaltender. He played a career total of 38 games in the National Hockey League (NHL). He played for the Detroit Red Wings. Dion would play 38 games with the Detroit Red Wings over parts of 2 seasons. After he left the NHL, Dion spent most of his career in the American Hockey League (AHL). In the AHL, he would play 39 games for the Indianapolis Capitals, 303 games over 6 seasons with the Buffalo Bisons, and 8 games with the St. Louis Flyers. During the 1949-50 season, Dion was able to win the Harry (Hap) Holmes Memorial Award for recording the lowest goals against average. Dion also played in the United States Hockey League (USHL). He played 7 games for the Houston Huskies and 4 games for the Louisville Blades. He retired from playing professional ice hockey in 1952. After he was hospitalized for 2 weeks, Dion died on 7 November 2014.

Connor McDavid (born January 13, 1997) is a Canadian professional ice hockey centre for the Edmonton Oilers of the National Hockey League (NHL) and serves as their captain. McDavid has been very successful throughout his NHL career. He is a six-time Art Ross Trophy winner, three-time Hart Memorial Trophy winner, five-time Ted Lindsay Award winner, one-time Maurice "Rocket" Richard Trophy winner, and a one-time Conn Smythe Trophy winner. McDavid is also a seven-time All-Star. He was the first overall pick in the 2015 NHL entry draft. He was the cover athlete for EA Sports' NHL 18. Internationally, McDavid plays for Canada and won a silver medal in 2026.

Cornelius Lance Hawkins (July 17, 1942 – October 6, 2017) was an American American Basketball League, National Basketball Association and American Basketball Association player, Harlem Globetrotter, Harlem Wizard and New York City playground legend. It was on the New York City courts that he earned his nickname The Hawk. Hawkins was born in Brooklyn, New York. He studied at Iowa State University.
Connor Metcalfe (born 5 November 1999) is an Australian soccer player. He plays for FC St. Pauli in the Bundesliga and for the Australia men's national soccer team (nicknamed the "Socceroos").

Connor Bedard (born July 17, 2005) is a Canadian professional ice hockey centre. He currently plays for the Chicago Blackhawks of the National Hockey League (NHL) and serves as their captain. Bedard has been called a generational talent and was called "The Future of Hockey" by The Hockey News. During his time playing in the Western Hockey League (WHL), Bedard was awarded the Jim Piggott Memorial, the Bob Clarke and the Four Broncos Memorial Trophys. He would also win the Canadian Hockey League (CHL)'s Top Scorer and Player of the Year awards. Bedard plays international hockey with Canada. He played with the under-18 team for the 2021 tournament, and with the National junior team in the 2022 and 2023 tournaments. He would help Canada win a gold medal in all three tournaments. He won the very first IIHF Male Player of the Year Award in 2023. Before playing in the NHL, Bedard played parts of 3 seasons with the Regina Pats of the Western Hockey League (WHL). He would be drafted first overall by the Pats in the 2020 WHL Bantam Draft. Before the draft, Hockey Canada gave Bedard exceptional player status which let him play in the WHL a year early. Before playing for the Pats, Bedard would be loaned to the juniour team for HV71 of the Swedish Hockey League (SHL) in 2020. He would play with them while the WHL had play suspended because of the COVID-19 pandemic. The WHL would continue play in March 2021 and Bedard would return to play for the Pats. In his first season with the team, he won the Jim Piggott Memorial Trophy for rookie of the year. The next year, Bedard would finish the season with 51 goals, 49 assists, and 100 points. He also became the youngest player in the WHL to score 50 or more goals in a season and the third 16-year-old to record a 100-point season in the league. It was the first one in the 21st century. In the 2022–23 season, Bedard would record a points streak for 35 games and became the league's leading scorer over that time. The streak would be snapped after being unable to record a point in a 3-2 win against the Lethbridge Hurricanes on February 3, 2023. Bedard's exceptional performance in the league led to lots of attention on his games. While traveling to other team's arenas, they would often sellout. When the Pats played the Calgary Hitmen at the Scotiabank Saddledome (also home of the Calgary Flames), there was an attendance of 17,223. Normally, a Hitmen game would sell an average of around 3,500. At the end of the season, he would be awarded the Bob Clarke and the Four Broncos Memorial Trophys. He would also win the Canadian Hockey League (CHL)'s Top Scorer and Player of the Year awards. When the Chicago Blackhawks won the number one pick in the 2023 lottery, it was reported that the Blackhawks had already sold $2.5 million in season ticket packages in anticipation of the selection of Bedard. On June 28, 2023 at the 2023 NHL Entry Draft, the Chicago Blackhawks would select Bedard first overall. On July 17, Bedard would sign a three-year entry level contract with a $950,000 cap hit. On October 10, Bedard would make his NHL debut in a 4–2 win against the Pittsburgh Penguins. In the game, Bedard would record his first point in the NHL when he got an assist on a Ryan Donato goal. The next night, the Blackhawks would play the Boston Bruins and Bedard would score his first NHL goal in a 3–1 loss. On January 4, 2024, Bedard was named to the 2024 National Hockey League All-Star Game, becoming the youngest selection in NHL history. However, Bedard would be injured with a broken jaw after being hit by Brendan Smith during a game against the New Jersey Devils the next day. On July 17, 2026, Bedard signed a five-year, $75 million contract to stay with the Blackhawks. On September 15, the team named Bedard as the 37th captain in Blackhawks franchise history.

Connor Charles Hellebuyck (born May 19, 1993) is an American professional ice hockey goaltender. He currently plays for the Winnipeg Jets of the National Hockey League (NHL). Hellebuyck is a three-time Vezina Trophy winner, winning in 2020, 2024, and 2025. He is also a two-time William M. Jennings Trophy winner in 2024 and 2025, and a one-time Hart Memorial Trophy winner in 2025. Hellebuyck is a four-time All-Star, being named one in 2018, 2020, 2023, and 2024. Internationally, Hellebuyck plays for the United States. He is a one-time gold medal winner, winning in 2026. Before playing in the NHL, Hellebuyck played two years with the UMass Lowell River Hawks of Hockey East. He was drafted 130th overall by the Winnipeg Jets in the 2012 NHL entry draft. On April 5, 2014, Hellebuyck signed a three-year entry-level contract to join the Jets. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliates St. John's IceCaps and Manitoba Moose. On November 27, 2015, the Jets called him up and Hellebuyck made his NHL debut, stopping 14 of 15 shots in a 3–1 win against the Minnesota Wild. On December 27, Hellebuyck stopped all 30 shots he faced to earn his first NHL career shutout in a 1–0 win against the Pittsburgh Penguins. On July 24, 2017, Hellebuyck signed a one-year, $2.25 million contract to stay with the Jets. He was given the starting goaltender role after Steve Mason was injured and his play started to become inconsistent. On January 10, 2018, Hellebuyck was selected to play in his first All-Star game. Hellebuyck finished the regular season with a record of 44–11–9 record, which broke Pittsburgh Penguins player Tom Barrasso's record for most single-season wins by an American goaltender in the National Hockey League. He continued his success into the playoffs. He helped the Jets defeat the Minnesota Wild four games to one in the opening round. Throughout the series, Hellebuyck played very well, earning shutouts in Games 4 and 5. In the next round, the Jets faced the Nashville Predators. In Game 1, Hellebuyck stopped 47 shots against to set a franchise record in a 4–1 win. On July 12, 2018, Hellebuyck signed a six-year, $37 million contract to stay with the Jets. On December 30, 2019, Hellebuyck was selected for his second All-Star game. On September 21, 2020, Hellebuyck was awarded the Vezina Trophy and became the first player in Thrashers/Jets franchise history to win the award. On January 19, 2023, Hellebuyck was selected for his third All-Star game. On October 9, Hellebuyck signed a seven-year, $59.5 million contract to stay with the Jets. On April 19, 2024, Hellebuyck was awarded the William M. Jennings Trophy for having the least amount of goals scored against him with only 199 goals. He was also awarded the Vezina Trophy for a second time. On April 16, 2025, Hellebuyck won his second William M. Jennings Trophy, only allowing 191 goals. On June 12, 2025, Hellebuyck won both a third Vezina Trophy and also his first Hart Trophy.

Connor Brown (born January 14, 1994) is a Canadian professional ice hockey right winger. He currently plays for the New Jersey Devils of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the Toronto Maple Leafs, Ottawa Senators, Washington Capitals, and Edmonton Oilers. Before playing in the NHL, Brown played one season with the St. Michael's Buzzers of the Ontario Junior Hockey League (OJHL) and three seasons with the Erie Otters of the Ontario Hockey League (OHL). He had a successful time with his teams. With the Otters, he won the Eddie Powers Memorial Trophy as the OHL's top scorer, Red Tilson Trophy as the OHL's most valuable player, and Jim Mahon Memorial Trophy as the OHL's top scoring right winger. He was also named to the First All-Rookie Team and First All-Star Team. He was drafted 156th overall by the Toronto Maple Leafs of the 2012 NHL entry draft. On November 22, 2013, Brown signed a three-year, $2.1525 million entry-level contract to join the Leafs. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Toronto Marlies. On March 17, 2016, the Leafs called him up and Brown made his NHL debut in a 4–1 loss against the Florida Panthers. On March 21, he recorded his first NHL point after assisting on a Josh Leivo goal in a 5–1 win against the Calgary Flames. On March 24, Brown scored his first NHL goal on the powerplay against Frederik Andersen in a 6–5 overtime win against the Anaheim Ducks. On August 27, 2017, Brown signed a three-year, $6.3 million contract to stay with the Leafs. On July 1, 2019, the Leafs traded Brown along with Michael Carcone and Nikita Zaitsev to the Ottawa Senators in exchange for Cody Ceci, Ben Harpur, Aaron Luchuk, and a 2020 third-round draft pick. On October 22, 2020, Brown signed a three-year, $3.6 million contract to stay with the Senators. On July 13, 2022, the Senators traded Brown to the Washington Capitals in exchange for a 2024 second-round draft pick. He played four regular season games for the Capitals. On July 1, 2023, Brown signed a one-year, $4 million contract to join the Edmonton Oilers. On July 1, 2024, Brown signed a one-year, $1 million contract to stay with the Oilers. On July 1, 2025, Brown signed a four-year, $12 million contract to join the New Jersey Devils.

Connor Bradley Clattenburg (born May 2, 2005) is a Canadian professional ice hockey forward. He currently plays for the Bakersfield Condors of the American Hockey League (AHL) and is under contract as a prospect for the Edmonton Oilers of the National Hockey League (NHL). Before playing in the NHL, Clattenburg played two seasons with the Sault Ste. Marie Greyhounds and two seasons with the Flint Firebirds of the Ontario Hockey League (OHL). He was drafted 160th overall by Edmonton Oilers in the 2024 NHL entry draft. On December 23, 2024, Clattenburg signed a three-year entry-level contract to join the Flames. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliates Bakersfield Condors. On November 22, 2025, the Oilers called him up and Clattenburg made his NHL debut in a 6–3 win against the Florida Panthers. On November 25, Clattenburg scored his first NHL goal against Jacob Markström in a 8–3 loss against the Dallas Stars.

Connor Mackey (born September 12, 1996) is an American professional ice hockey defenseman. He currently plays for Rockford IceHogs of the American Hockey League (AHL) and is under contract with the Chicago Blackhawks of the National Hockey League (NHL). He also played for the Calgary Flames, Arizona Coyotes, and New York Rangers. Before playing in the NHL, Mackey played two seasons with the Green Bay Gamblers of the United States Hockey League (USHL) and three years with the Minnesota State Mavericks of the Western Collegiate Hockey Association (WCHA). He had a successful time with his teams. With the Gamblers, he was named the Defenseman of the Year and was also named to the First All-Star Team. With the Mavericks, he named to the WCHA All-Rookie Team, WCHA First All-Star Team, and WCHA Third All-Star Team. He was not drafted by an NHL team. On March 20, 2020, Mackey signed a three-year entry-level contract to join the Calgary Flames of the National Hockey League (NHL). On February 13, 2021, Mackey made his NHL debut in a 3–1 loss against the Vancouver Canucks. Two days later on February 15, he recorded his first NHL point after assisting on a Milan Lucic goal in a 4–3 overtime win against the Vancouver Canucks. On May 19, Mackey scored his first NHL goal against Braden Holtby in a 6–2 win against the Vancouver Canucks. On September 8, 2021, Mackey signed a two-year contract to stay with the Flames. On March 3, 2023, the Flames traded Mackey along with Brett Ritchie to the Arizona Coyotes in exchange for Nick Ritchie and Troy Stecher. He scored 1 goal and recorded 3 assists in 20 regular season games with the Coyotes. On July 1, 2023, Mackey signed a one-year contract to join the New York Rangers. On July 1, 2023, Mackey signed a one-year contract to stay with the Rangers. He played five regular season games over three seasons with the Rangers. On July 1, 2026, Mackey signed a one-year contract to join the Chicago Blackhawks.

Connor Murphy (born March 26, 1993) is an American professional ice hockey defenseman. He currently plays for the Edmonton Oilers of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the Phoenix/Arizona Coyotes and Chicago Blackhawks. Before playing in the NHL, Murphy played parts of two seasons with the U.S. National Development Team of the United States Hockey League (USHL) and two years with the Sarnia Sting of the Ontario Hockey League (OHL). He was drafted 20th overall by the Phoenix Coyotes in the 2011 NHL entry draft. On August 4, 2011, Murphy signed a three-year, $2.775 million entry-level contract to join the Coyotes. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Portland Pirates. On November 16, 2013, the Coyotes called him up and Murphy made his NHL debut in a 6–2 win against the Tampa Bay Lightning. During the second period, he scored his first NHL goal against Anders Lindbäck. On July 28, 2016, Murphy signed a six-year, $23.1 million entry-level contract to stay with the Coyotes. On June 23, 2017, the Coyotes traded Murphy along with Laurent Dauphin to the Chicago Blackhawks in exchange for Niklas Hjalmarsson. On August 31, 2021, Murphy signed a four-year, $17.6 million contract to stay with the Blackhawks. On March 2, 2026, the Blackhawks traded Murphy and retained 50% of his contract to the Edmonton Oilers in exchange for a 2028 second-round draft pick. On June 22, 2026, Murphy signed a five-year, $20.5 million contract to stay with the Oilers.

Ryan Parmeter (born February 6, 1980) is an American professional wrestler. He wrestles under the ring name Kon. He is best known for his work in WWE, where he wrestled under the ring names Conor O'Brian and Konnor. He was part of the fourth season of NXT and placed fourth on the fifth season of NXT. Parmeter also competed in Total Nonstop Action Wrestling (TNA) He was formerly in WWE from 2005 to 2008, but both Parmeter and his girlfriend who was also employed with the company asked for their released due to health problems. He was re-signed by the WWE on July 14, 2010 and was sent to their FCW developmental territory. He competed on the fourth season of NXT but was the second person eliminated. He also competed on the fifth season of NXT titled NXT Redemption but was eliminated fourth. Parmeter won the NXT Tag Team Championship with Viktor on September 12, 2013, when they defeated Adrian Neville and Corey Graves. They were the longest reigning NXT Tag Team Champions of all time, holding the titles for 364 days. ARW Tag Team Championship (1 time) – with Vik CCW Tag Team Championship (1 time) – with Sean Allen FSCW Tag Team Championship (1 time) – with Jeff "J-Dawg" Brooks IWR World Heavyweight Championship (1 time) NWA Sunray Heavyweight Championship (1 time) PWI ranked him No. 123 of the top 500 singles wrestlers in the PWI 500 in 2014 NXT Tag Team Championship (1 time) – with Viktor

Conor Anthony McGregor (born 14 July 1988) is an Irish mixed martial artist and boxer. He started his career in 2008. He is signed to the Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC). He is the former UFC Featherweight Champion and UFC Lightweight Champion. He has fought as a featherweight, lightweight and welterweight. At UFC 194, he defeated Jose Aldo to win the UFC featherweight championship. In his welterweight debut at UFC 196, he was defeated by Nate Diaz in the second round via submission. On 6 October 2018, he won the UFC lightweight championship by defeating Eddie Alvarez and won via KO. In his boxing debut in 2017, he was defeated by Floyd Mayweather Jr.. He returned to MMA in 2018 and was defeated by Khabib Nurmagomedov via submission at UFC 229. The event set the record for the biggest MMA pay-per-view event, with 2.4 million buys in the United States. Throughout his career, McGregor has become the subject of many controversies due to his behaviour. In March 2025, McGregor announced his independent campaign for President of Ireland in the 2025 election. He dropped out of the race in September 2025. McGregor was born in Dublin. His parents are Timmy and Súsan McGregor. He started kickboxing in 2008, the same year he started dating his girlfriend Dee Devlin. Their son, Conor Jack McGregor, was born in May 2017. In 2019, McGregor was investigated for two separate sexual assaults. Prosecutors said they were not going to charge him for the first one. McGregor's spokesperson said that he rejected the allegations. A woman named Nikita Hand filed a lawsuit against McGregor and claimed that he had beat and raped her in a Dublin hotel in October 2018. On 22 November 2024, a jury found McGregor guilty of raping Hand. The judge ordered McGregor to pay for Hand's legal fees. McGregor said that he was appealing the verdict. After the verdict, McGregor lost many sponsorship deals and his alcohol was pulled from bars and store shelves.

Connor Zary (born September 25, 2001) is a Canadian professional ice hockey centre. He currently plays for the Calgary Flames of the National Hockey League (NHL). Before playing in the NHL, Zary played four seasons with the Kamloops Blazers of the Western Hockey League (WHL). He was drafted 24th overall by the Calgary Flames in the 2020 NHL entry draft. On December 31, Zary signed a three-year, $925,000 entry-level contract to join the Flames. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliates Stockton Heat and Calgary Wranglers. On November 1, 2023, the Flames called him up and Zary made his NHL debut in a 4–3 loss against the Dallas Stars. During the game, Zary scored his first NHL goal against Jake Oettinger. On September 6, 2025, Zary signed a three-year, $11.3 million contract to stay with the Flames.

Conor Garland (born March 11, 1996) is an American professional ice hockey winger. He currently plays for the Columbus Blue Jackets of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the Arizona Coyotes and Vancouver Canucks. Before playing in the NHL, Garland played six regular season games with the Muskegon Lumberjacks of the United States Hockey League (USHL) and four seasons with the Moncton Wildcats of the Quebec Major Junior Hockey League (QMJHL). He had a successful time with his teams. With the Wildcats, he won the Jean Béliveau Trophy as the QMJHL's top scorer, the Michel Brière Memorial Trophy as the QMJHL's most valuable player, and was named the CHL Top Scorer Award. He was also named to the First All-Star Team. He was drafted 123rd overall by the Arizona Coyotes in the 2015 NHL entry draft. On December 23, 2015, Garland signed a three-year entry-level contract to join the Coyotes. On January 26, 2021, Garland made his NHL debut in a 5–3 loss against the San Jose Sharks. On October 16, Garland scored his first NHL goal against Philipp Grubauer in a 6–4 win against the Colorado Avalanche. On February 27, 2019, Garland signed a two-year, $1.55 million contract to stay with the Coyotes. On July 23, 2021, the Coyotes traded Garland along with Oliver Ekman-Larsson to the Vancouver Canucks in exchange for Loui Eriksson, Antoine Roussel, Jay Beagle, a 2021 first-round draft pick, a 2022 second-round draft pick, and a 2023 seventh-round draft pick. On July 27, 2021, Garland signed a five-year, $24.75 million contract to stay with the Canucks. He played five seasons with the Canucks. On March 6, 2026, the Canucks traded Garland to the Columbus Blue Jackets in exchange for a 2026 third-round draft pick and a 2028 second-round draft pick.

Conor Michael Sheary (born June 8, 1992) is an American professional ice hockey winger. He currently plays for the Buffalo Sabres of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the Pittsburgh Penguins, Washington Capitals, Tampa Bay Lightning, and New York Rangers. Sheary is a two-time Stanley Cup champion, winning back-to-back with the Penguins in 2016 and 2017. Before playing in the NHL, Sheary played four years with the UMass Minutemen of Hockey East. He was not drafted by an NHL team. On July 1, 2015, Sheary signed a three-year entry-level contract to join the Pittsburgh Penguins of the National Hockey League (NHL). He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Wilkes-Barre/Scranton Penguins. On December 16, 2015, Pittsburgh called him up and Sheary made his NHL debut in a 3–0 loss against the Boston Bruins. Two days later on December 18, Sheary scored his first NHL goal against Tuukka Rask in a 6–2 loss against the Boston Bruins. He also recorded an assist on a Trevor Daley goal. He helped the Penguins during the playoffs. They defeated the New York Rangers, Washington Capitals, and Tampa Bay Lightning. They eventually went on to defeat the San Jose Sharks four games to two in the Finals to win the Stanley Cup. On January 23, 2017, the league named him as the First Star of the Week. That season, he helped the team reach their second-straight Finals, as the Penguins went on to defeat the Nashville Predators four games to two to win repeat as Stanley Cup champions. On July 30, 2017, Sheary signed a three-year, $9 million contract to stay with the Penguins. On June 27, 2018, the Penguins traded Sheary along with Matt Hunwick to the Buffalo Sabres in exchange for a 2019 conditional fourth-round draft pick. He played two seasons with the Sabres. On February 24, 2020, the Sabres traded Sheary along with Evan Rodrigues back to the Pittsburgh Penguins in exchange for the Dominik Kahun. He scored 1 goal and recorded 3 assists in 8 regular season games, as well as, recording 2 assists in four playoff games in his return with the Penguins. On December 22, 2020, Sheary signed a one-year, $735,000 contract to join the Washington Capitals. On April 14, 2021, Sheary signed a two-year, $3 million to stay with the Capitals. On July 1, 2023, Sheary signed a three-year, $6 million contract to join the Tampa Bay Lightning. He played two seasons with the Lightning. On June 29, 2025, the Lightning placed Sheary onto waivers and terminated his contract. On October 6, 2025, Sheary signed a one-year contract to join the New York Rangers. He scored seven goals and eleven assists in 62 regular season games with the Rangers. On July 1, 2026, Sheary signed a one-year, $850,000 contract to rejoin the Buffalo Sabres.

Conrad "Cronos" Lant (15 January 1963 – 29 September 2026) was the vocalist and bass player in black metal band Venom. He was born in 1963 in London, England. Cronos started to sing in 1978 in the band Guillotine. Then he knew Jeffrey "Mantas" Dunn and they founded Venom. In 1989 Cronos left the band to start a solo work. Venom could not go on without him and they stopped singing in 1993. Then Cronos returned in 1995 and rejoined the band. On 1 October 2026, Cronos' bandmates Rage and Danté and his son Nathan announced on social media that Cronos had died at the age of 63. No cause of death has been given.

José Conrado Miranda Sasso (14 October 1928 – 13 October 2021) was a Salvadoran footballer and manager. He made 20 appearances for the El Salvador national football team between 1948 until 1955. He would also coach for them four times in 1961, 1971, 1975 and 1989. Miranda died on 13 October 2021 at a hospital in San Salvador from cardiopulmonary arrest caused by COVID-19, aged 92.

Constantin "Costel" Rădulescu (5 October 1896 – 14 June 1981) was a Romanian footballer, manager, and referee. Between 1923 and 1938 he worked with the Romanian Football Federation as an administrator and the manager of the Romania national team. He later worked as a referee for 20 years in the Divizia A. Rădulescu died on 14 June 1981 at age 84. Central European International Cup: 1931–34 Manager with the most Balkan Cup titles: 3 titles

Cooper DeJean (Born February 9, 2003) is an American football player for the Philadelphia Eagles of the National Football League (NFL). He plays the cornerback position. He played college football at the University of Iowa. He was selected in the second round of the 2024 NFL Draft.

Cor Hildebrand (13 September 1951 – 16 August 2022) was a Dutch footballer. Hildebrand started playing with VV DOS and played 16 matches in the 1969–70 season. The club merged into FC Utrecht the next season. He played eight seasons for FC Utrecht at the highest level playing 174 matches. In between, he played one season on loan for FC Wageningen (1976–77) in the first division. He retired after the 1978–79 season. Hildebrand died in Utrecht on 16 August 2022, aged 70. In the following home match of FC Utrecht against AFC Ajax, a minute of silence was held for him.

Cornelius "Cor" van der Hoeven (12 May 1921 – 1 February 2017) was a Dutch footballer. He played as a midfielder for DWS and Ajax. He also made three appearances with the national team. He was born in Amsterdam. Van der Hoeven died on 1 February 2017 in Amsterdam at the age of 95.

Corey Crawford (born December 31, 1984) is a Canadian former professional ice hockey goaltender. He played a total 10 seasons in the National Hockey League (NHL). He played his entire career for the Chicago Blackhawks. He made his debut with the Blackhawks on January 22, 2006 against the Minnesota Wild. Crawford also played in the QMJHL for the Moncton Wildcats. On June 24, 2013, He won the Stanley Cup with the Blackhawks after they defeated the Boston Bruins 4 games to 2 in the 2013 Stanley Cup Finals. On October 9, 2020, Crawford signed a two-year, $7.8 million contract with the New Jersey Devils. However, he never played for them. On January 9, 2021, Crawford announced that he was retiring from professional ice hockey. Stanley Cup (2013) - with the Chicago Blackhawks William M. Jennings Trophy (shared with Ray Emery) (2012-13) NHL Second Star of the Week of Jan. 19–27 2013 QMJHL Telus Defensive Player of the Year (2003-04)

Corey Michael Locke (born May 8, 1984) is a Canadian former professional ice hockey player. He played nine games in the National Hockey League (NHL). He played for the Montreal Canadiens, New York Rangers, and Ottawa Senators. He also played for TPS of the SM-liiga (SM-l). He was born in Newmarket, Ontario. He retired from playing professional ice hockey in 2019.

Matt Polinsky (born February 24, 1984) is an American retired professional wrestler. He is better known by his ring name Corey Graves. He is currently signed to the WWE and works as a commentator for SmackDown. During his career, Polinsky was a one-time NXT Tag Team Champion with Adrian Neville. He is also known for his work on the independent circuit where he competed under the ring name Sterling James Keenan. On December 11 2014, during the pre-show of NXT Takeover: R Evolution, Graves announced that he was officially retiring from in-ring competition because of his concussion issues. Graves would then announce that he would join the NXT commentary team and that he would start at the beginning at the event. He was given a two-year contract by Triple H, which gives him a shot at becoming a guest commentator for either Raw, SmackDown or pay-per-views.
